translations.idiomatic: Loyalty and Righteousness, Part Two

translations.idiomatic: Ma Hongru et al.

translations.literal: Deng Deng
translations.idiomatic: Deng Deng

translations.literal: Xiao Zhen and others; Cui Chenglan; Huang Xinde
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zhen et al.; Cui Chenglan; Huang Xinde

translations.literal: Sui Guangqi and others
translations.idiomatic: Sui Guangqi et al.

sentences.zh: 馬秉倫劉鎮寶

translations.literal: Ma Binglun; Liu Zhenbao
translations.idiomatic: Ma Binglun; Liu Zhenbao

sentences.zh: 朱國治，漢軍正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Zhu Guozhi was a Han military bannerman of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Guozhi belonged to the Plain Yellow Banner of the Han military divisions.

sentences.zh: 順治四年，由貢生授固安知縣，屢擢至大理寺卿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shunzhi, he was appointed magistrate of Gu'an as a tribute student and was repeatedly promoted to Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 4, appointed Gu'an magistrate through the tribute-student route, he rose by stages to Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 十六年，外簡江寧巡撫。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, he was selected from outside the capital to serve as Governor of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was posted from outside the regular roster as Jiangning governor.

sentences.zh: 時鄭成功盤踞外洋，出沒江南濱海州縣，國治疏言：「欲破狡謀，先度形勢。

translations.literal: At that time Zheng Chenggong held the outer seas and raided coastal prefectures and counties of Jiangnan; Guozhi memorialized: "To break his cunning schemes, one must first assess the strategic situation.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chenggong then dominated the open sea and struck Jiangnan's coastal prefectures and counties; Guozhi submitted: "To break his stratagems, weigh the situation first.

sentences.zh: 賊眾負險，我師遠涉風濤，其勞逸不同。

translations.literal: The rebels rely on dangerous terrain while our army crosses distant wind and waves—their ease and our fatigue differ.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels hold defensible ground; our men cross stormy seas—a mismatch of ease and exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 賊眾熟識海道，我師弓馬便捷，其素習不同；

translations.literal: The rebels know the sea routes well, while our army is skilled in bow and horse—their long practice and ours differ;
translations.idiomatic: They know every sea lane; we excel on horseback and with the bow—their training and ours differ;

sentences.zh: 水師舟楫，較之賊船大小懸殊，其攻取不同。

translations.literal: Our naval vessels, compared with rebel ships, differ vastly in size—our method of attack differs.
translations.idiomatic: Our war junks dwarf theirs in every dimension—so the way we fight must differ too.

sentences.zh: 臣謂宜以守寓戰，凡海邊江口，多設墩台，待賊勢困援絕，乘間攻之，自能擒渠獻馘。」

translations.literal: Your subject holds that defense should embody offense: set watch towers thickly at every seaside mouth and river entrance, wait until the rebels are weary and cut off from aid, then strike at the chance—you will capture the ringleader and offer his head.
translations.idiomatic: I counsel defending as fighting: tower every river mouth and coast, wait until the rebels are spent and isolated, then strike—you will take their chief and present his head.

sentences.zh: 下所司議行。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the responsible office for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the ministries for action.

sentences.zh: 又以蘇、松、常、鎮四府錢糧抗欠者多，分別造冊，紳士一萬三千五百餘人，衙役二百四十人，請敕部察議。

translations.literal: Further, because in the four prefectures of Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, and Zhenjiang many grain and tax payments were in arrears, separate registers were drawn up listing more than 13,500 gentlemen and 240 yamen runners; he requested that the ministries investigate and decide.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted heavy tax arrears in Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, and Zhenjiang, drew separate rolls of more than 13,500 gentry and 240 runners, and asked the ministries to rule.

sentences.zh: 部議現任官降二級調用，衿士褫革，衙役照贓治罪有差。

translations.literal: The ministry ruled that incumbent officials be demoted two ranks and transferred, gentlemen stripped of rank, and yamen runners punished for theft according to respective degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries ordered serving officials cut two grades and transferred, degree-holders degraded, and runners punished as robbers by degree.

sentences.zh: 以是頗有刻覈名。

translations.literal: Because of this he gained quite a reputation for severity.
translations.idiomatic: He earned a reputation for stern exactitude.

sentences.zh: 康熙十年，補雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kangxi, he was appointed Governor of Yunnan to fill a vacancy.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 10 brought appointment as Yunnan governor.

sentences.zh: 時吳三桂謀叛久矣，十二年，詭請移籓錦州，並期以十一月二十四日啟行。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui had long been plotting rebellion; in the twelfth year he falsely requested transfer of his fief to Jinzhou and set the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month for departure.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui had plotted for years; in Kangxi 12 he feigned a request to move his fief to Jinzhou, fixing departure for the eleventh month's twenty-fourth day.

sentences.zh: 國治方請增設驛堡，協撥夫馬待之，三桂遽踞關隘起事。

translations.literal: Guozhi was just requesting additional courier stations and coordinated allocation of porters and horses to receive him when Sangui suddenly seized the passes and rose in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: While Guozhi was still arranging courier posts and draft animals for the move, Sangui seized the passes and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 先期三日，邀國治及按察使李興元、雲南知府高顯辰、同知劉琨，脅之從逆，皆不屈。

translations.literal: Three days before the scheduled date, he invited Guozhi and Regional Inspector Li Xingyuan, Yunnan Prefect Gao Xianchen, and Vice-Prefect Liu Kun, coercing them to join the rebellion; all refused.
translations.idiomatic: Three days early he summoned Guozhi, Inspector Li Xingyuan, Prefect Gao Xianchen, and Vice-Prefect Liu Kun to follow him; all refused.

sentences.zh: 國治罵賊尤烈，即時遇害。

translations.literal: Guozhi cursed the rebels with especial vehemence and was killed on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhi reviled them most bitterly and was killed at once.

sentences.zh: 先後殉難者，雲貴總督甘文焜，廣西巡撫馬雄鎮、傅弘烈及李興元，均自有傳。

translations.literal: Others who died martyrs around the same time were Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Gan Wenxuan; Guangxi Governor Ma Xiongzhen, Fu Honglie, and Li Xingyuan—each has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Other martyrs in Yunnan included Governor-General Gan Wenxuan and Guangxi governors Ma Xiongzhen and Fu Honglie, with Li Xingyuan—all have separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 楊應鶚，鑲黃旗漢軍。

translations.literal: Yang Ying'e was a Han bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ying'e belonged to the Bordered Yellow Banner of the Han divisions.

sentences.zh: 任貴州貴陽府同知。

translations.literal: He served as Vice-Prefect of Guiyang Prefecture in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He held the Guiyang prefectural vice-magistracy in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂初叛，執應鶚送雲南，錮之順寧。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui first rebelled, he seized Ying'e and sent him to Yunnan, imprisoning him at Shunning.
translations.idiomatic: At Wu Sangui's first rising he was seized and sent to Yunnan, then locked at Shunning.

sentences.zh: 應鶚密謀舉義，偽將軍趙永寧縊死之。

translations.literal: Ying'e secretly plotted an uprising; the rebel general Zhao Yongning had him strangled.
translations.idiomatic: Ying'e plotted secretly to rise; the rebel general Zhao Yongning strangled him.

sentences.zh: 時有馬弘儒者，順治十八年武進士。

translations.literal: At the time there was Ma Hongru, a military metropolitan graduate of the eighteenth year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Among them was Ma Hongru, military jinshi of Shunzhi 18.

sentences.zh: 三桂素重之，迫共叛，不聽，以鐵椎椎其齒，齒盡落，囚琨明，不屈死。

translations.literal: Sangui had long esteemed him and forced him to rebel together; he would not listen; they hammered his teeth out with an iron mallet until all fell, imprisoned him at Kunming, and he died unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui valued him and pressed him to rebel; he refused; they smashed his teeth with an iron pestle until none remained, kept him in Kunming prison, and he died defiant.

sentences.zh: 先後在滇殉節者，為鄭相等：相，江寧人，以中書隨軍至雲南。

translations.literal: Those who died loyal in Yunnan thereafter included Zheng Xiang: Xiang, a man of Jiangning, went to Yunnan as a Secretariat drafter with the army.
translations.idiomatic: Others who perished in Yunnan included Zheng Xiang of Jiangning, who had gone south as a Secretariat drafter with the army.

sentences.zh: 大兵入滇，檄權石屏州事，有惠政。

translations.literal: When the imperial army entered Yunnan, he was ordered to act as magistrate of Shiping, and his benevolent policies won favor.
translations.idiomatic: When imperial forces entered Yunnan he was placed in charge of Shiping with policies the people welcomed.

sentences.zh: 偽總兵高應鳳作亂，相死之。

translations.literal: The rebel commander Gao Yingfeng rose in disorder and Xiang died defending the post.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel regional commander Gao Yingfeng revolted; Xiang died at his post.

sentences.zh: 琨明人楊樹烈，以四川南川縣知縣告休家居，寇至，北面再拜，自縊死。

translations.literal: Yang Shulie of Kunming had retired as magistrate of Nanchuan County in Sichuan; when bandits came he bowed to the north twice and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shulie of Kunming, retired Nanchuan magistrate in Sichuan, bowed north twice and hanged himself when rebels came.

sentences.zh: 土酋龍韜等分道剽掠，寧州知州曹誠嬰城守，城陷死之。

translations.literal: Tribal chiefs Long Tao and others plundered by separate routes; Ningzhou Magistrate Cao Cheng defended the city under siege and died when it fell.
translations.idiomatic: Chieftains such as Long Tao raided on several routes; Ningzhou magistrate Cao Cheng held the walls and died when the city fell.

sentences.zh: 原任曲靖府教授周起元，則以被執不屈死。

translations.literal: Former Qujing Prefecture Instructor Zhou Qiyuan died refusing submission after capture.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qujing instructor Zhou Qiyuan was taken and died rather than submit.

sentences.zh: 生員有唐方齡、張鶤羽。

translations.literal: Among students were Tang Fangling and Zhang Heyu.
translations.idiomatic: Student martyrs included Tang Fangling and Zhang Heyu.

sentences.zh: 三桂既叛，所在蠢應，死貴州者：陳上年，直隸清苑人。

translations.literal: Once Sangui rebelled, responses sprang up everywhere; those who died in Guizhou included Chen Shangnian of Qingyuan in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: After Sangui's revolt the provinces erupted; in Guizhou Chen Shangnian of Zhili's Qingyuan died.

sentences.zh: 順治六年進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate of the sixth year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He had passed the civil examinations in Shunzhi 6.

sentences.zh: 時官分巡右江參議道，三桂既執巡撫傅弘烈，乃脅上年降，幽縶死。

translations.literal: He then held the post of Circuit Intendant touring the Right River; after Sangui seized Governor Fu Honglie, he compelled Shangnian to submit; Shangnian was imprisoned and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was Right River intendant when Sangui took Fu Honglie and tried to force Shangnian over; Shangnian was clapped in irons and died there.

sentences.zh: 都勻縣防兵謀應賊，譁譟焚掠，知縣薛佩玉諭以順逆，眾不聽，偪受偽職。

translations.literal: Garrison soldiers of Duyun plotted to join the rebels, rioted and looted by fire; Magistrate Xue Peiyu instructed them on loyalty and treason, but the crowd would not listen and forced him to accept a false post.
translations.idiomatic: Duyun's militia mutinied and burned the town; magistrate Xue Peiyu preached loyalty and treason; they ignored him and pressed a false appointment on him.

sentences.zh: 佩玉北面再拜，自縊死。

translations.literal: Peiyu bowed to the north twice and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Peiyu bowed north twice and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 死湖廣者：祝昌，河南固始人。

translations.literal: Those who died in Huguang: Zhu Chang of Gushi in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In Huguang, Zhu Chang of Henan's Gushi died.

sentences.zh: 順治六年進士，由中書累擢至辰沅道。

translations.literal: Metropolitan graduate of Shunzhi 6; from Secretariat drafter he rose by stages to Chen-Yuan Circuit Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi 6 jinshi; he rose from Secretariat drafter to Chen-Yuan intendant.

sentences.zh: 三桂叛聞，即流涕諭眾大義，皆感泣。

translations.literal: On hearing of Sangui's rebellion he wept and instructed the people in the great obligation; all were moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the rebellion he wept and preached duty; the whole crowd wept with him.

sentences.zh: 賊大至，城潰，北面再拜自縊死。

translations.literal: When the rebels came in force the city was breached; he bowed to the north twice and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels overran the walls; he bowed north twice and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 生員有李廷員、張一元、徐翹楚。

translations.literal: Among students were Li Tingyuan, Zhang Yiyuan, and Xu Qiaochu.
translations.idiomatic: Student martyrs included Li Tingyuan, Zhang Yiyuan, and Xu Qiaochu.

sentences.zh: 死江西者：為饒州府知府郭萬國，萬年縣知縣王萬鎰。

translations.literal: Those who died in Jiangxi: Raozhou Prefect Guo Wanguo and Wannian County Magistrate Wang Wanyin.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangxi, Raozhou prefect Guo Wanguo and Wannian magistrate Wang Wanyin died.

sentences.zh: 萬國，河南許州人。

translations.literal: Wanguo was a man of Xuzhou in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Wanguo came from Henan's Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 由諸生從經略洪承疇官貴州，撫苗、蠻有功。

translations.literal: From private student he followed Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou to Guizhou and pacified the Miao and Man with merit.
translations.idiomatic: A licentiate who followed Hong Chengchou to Guizhou, he pacified Miao and Man tribes with credit.

sentences.zh: 萬鎰，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Wanyin was a man of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyin was from Zhejiang's Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 由貢生官福建，平土賊有功。

translations.literal: From tribute student he served in Fujian and pacified native bandits with merit.
translations.idiomatic: As tribute student in Fujian he suppressed native brigands with credit.

sentences.zh: 賊黨圍廣信急，覘饒州備虛，由間道薄城。

translations.literal: Rebel bands besieged Guangxin urgently, saw Raozhou's defenses thin, and by a side path pressed on the city.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels besieged Guangxin hard, saw Raozhou undefended, and stole toward it by a back road.

sentences.zh: 萬國令萬鎰赴省請援，甫出北門，賊猝至，與家僮六人中砲歿。

translations.literal: Wanguo ordered Wanyin to go to the provincial capital for aid; he had just passed the north gate when rebels arrived suddenly; he and six household servants died by cannon.
translations.idiomatic: Wanguo sent Wanyin to the capital for help; just outside the north gate rebels struck; he and six servants fell to cannon fire.

sentences.zh: 饒州營參將趙登舉聞警馳救，衝賊營，擒前隊數人，伏起，陣亡。

translations.literal: Raozhou garrison Vice Commander Zhao Dengju heard the alarm and raced to the rescue, charged the rebel camp, captured several in the van, but when ambush rose he fell in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commander Zhao Dengju charged the rebel camp and took prisoners in the van; ambushers rose and he fell.

sentences.zh: 賊黨環城招降，萬國集其屬同知範之英、鄱陽縣知縣陸之蕃、石門巡檢翁鳳翥、饒州稅課大使李崇道，謂之曰：「文臣不習戰，然守土吏當死，不可徒手就戮。」

translations.literal: Rebel bands surrounded the city calling for surrender; Wanguo gathered his subordinates Vice Magistrate Fan Zhiying, Poyang Magistrate Lu Zhifan, Shimen Sub-Prefect Weng Fengzhu, and Raozhou Tax Commissioner Li Chongdao, telling them: "Civil officials do not practice warfare, yet officials who hold the soil must die—we cannot go unarmed to be slaughtered."
translations.idiomatic: Rebels ringed the city summoning surrender; Wanguo gathered Fan Zhiying, Lu Zhifan, Weng Fengzhu, and Li Chongdao and said: "We are civil men, yet holders of the land must die—not walk unarmed to slaughter."

sentences.zh: 皆應之。

translations.literal: All answered yes.
translations.idiomatic: All agreed.

sentences.zh: 賊偪靈芝門，攀堞登，萬國率家丁巷戰，身先之，中十六創，與之蕃、鳳翥、崇道俱戰歿。

translations.literal: Rebels pressed the Lingzhi Gate, climbed the battlements; Wanguo led household retainers in street fighting, taking the lead, received sixteen wounds, and fell in battle together with Zhifan, Fengzhu, and Chongdao.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels forced Lingzhi Gate and scaled the wall; Wanguo led retainers in lane fighting, took sixteen wounds, and fell with Zhifan, Fengzhu, and Chongdao.

sentences.zh: 文英亦被執不屈死。

translations.literal: Zhiying was also seized and died unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiying too was captured and died defiant.

sentences.zh: 萍鄉民人彭程淑，亦​​以三桂餘黨擾其鄉，裂眥怒罵，被亂刃死。

translations.literal: Peng Chengshu, a commoner of Pingxiang, was also killed by rebel blades when, eyes split with rage, he cursed the remnant bands of Sangui disturbing his village.
translations.idiomatic: Pingxiang commoner Peng Chengshu cursed Sangui's remnant bands raiding his village with bloodshot eyes and was cut down.

sentences.zh: 死廣東者：金世爵，鑲藍旗漢軍。

translations.literal: Those who died in Guangdong: Jin Shijue, a Han bannerman of the Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangdong, Jin Shijue of the Bordered Blue Han Banner died.

sentences.zh: 由舉人任合浦縣知縣。

translations.literal: From provincial graduate he served as magistrate of Hepu County.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate, he was Hepu magistrate.

sentences.zh: 高州總兵祖澤清叛附三桂，世爵圖城守。

translations.literal: Gaozhou Regional Commander Zu Zeqing rebelled and joined Sangui; Shijue prepared to defend the city.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozhou commander Zu Zeqing rebelled; Shijue braced to hold the walls.

sentences.zh: 偽將王弘勳率賊數万犯廉州，世爵登陴力禦，城陷，與守備杜嶠同死之。

translations.literal: The rebel general Wang Hongxun led tens of thousands against Lianzhou; Shijue mounted the walls and fought fiercely; when the city fell he and garrison commander Du Jiao died together.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel Wang Hongxun led myriads against Lianzhou; Shijue fought from the parapet; when the city fell he and defender Du Jiao died together.

sentences.zh: 又侯進學者，隸平南王尚可喜籓下。

translations.literal: There was also Hou Jinxue, under the fief of Prince of Pingnan Shang Kexi.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jinxue served under Prince of Pingnan Shang Kexi.

sentences.zh: 先為三桂所脅，為遞逆書，至廣州自首，可喜以聞，嘉之，授世職。

translations.literal: First coerced by Sangui to carry a treasonous dispatch, he went to Guangzhou to surrender himself; Kexi reported it, the court praised him, and he was granted a hereditary post.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui had once forced him to carry a rebel message; he surrendered at Guangzhou; Kexi reported it and the throne rewarded him with a hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 至是為賊所得，囚木籠送常德，三桂臠之於市。

translations.literal: Now seized by rebels, he was caged in timber and sent to Changde; Sangui dismembered him in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Now captured, he was sent to Changde in a wooden cage; Sangui quartered him in the market.

sentences.zh: 逆黨馬雄攻新會，籓下諸將多附逆，誘左翼游擊文天壽同降，天壽叱之曰：「背主不忠！

translations.literal: Rebel Ma Xiong attacked Xinhui; many fief generals went over, tempting Left Wing Guerrilla Commander Wen Tianshou to join; Tianshou rebuked them: "Betraying one's lord is disloyalty!
translations.idiomatic: Rebel Ma Xiong took Xinhui; fief generals tempted Left Wing guerrilla Wen Tianshou to defect; he thundered: "Betrayal is disloyalty!

sentences.zh: 吾錚錚丈夫，豈鼠輩可脅？」

translations.literal: I am a resolute man—how can vermin threaten me?
translations.idiomatic: I am no mouse a rabble can frighten—

sentences.zh: 遂被害，沉屍海中。

translations.literal: He was then killed and his body cast into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: and was killed, his corpse thrown into the sea.

sentences.zh: 死川、陝者：波羅營副將張國彥，聞提督王輔臣叛，城守。

translations.literal: Those who died in Sichuan and Shaanxi: Boluo Garrison Vice Commander Zhang Guoyan, on hearing Regional Commander Wang Fuchen rebel, held the city.
translations.idiomatic: In Sichuan and Shaanxi, Boluo vice commander Zhang Guoyan heard Wang Fuchen rebel and closed the gates.

sentences.zh: 兵變，逼獻印，自刎死。

translations.literal: The troops mutinied and forced him to surrender the seal; he cut his throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: Troops mutinied, demanding the seal; he cut his throat.

sentences.zh: 漢中城陷，同知汪化鼇不受偽職，賊縶之，复給偽劄令攝縣事。

translations.literal: When Hanzhong fell, Vice Prefect Wang Hu'ao refused a false post; rebels bound him, then again gave a false commission ordering him to administer the county.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhong fell; vice prefect Wang Hu'ao refused rebel office; they bound him, then offered a forged commission to rule the county.

sentences.zh: 化鼇痛哭，望闕遙拜，自縊死。

translations.literal: Hu'ao wept, bowed toward the palace from afar, and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He wept, bowed toward the capital, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 漢鳳參將蘇興亦叛附三桂，將襲殺诇賊筆帖式布格爾以滅口。

translations.literal: Hanfeng Vice Commander Su Xing also rebelled with Sangui and was about to assassinate scout-clerk Bugur to silence him.
translations.idiomatic: Hanfeng vice commander Su Xing joined Sangui and planned to kill scout Bugur to silence him.

sentences.zh: 千總魯仁圻憤甚，度無以製之，朝衣拜父像告訣，叩營力爭，觸興怒，殺之。

translations.literal: Thousand-Commander Lu Renqi was greatly enraged, saw no way to restrain him, donned court robes to bow before his father's portrait in farewell, went to the camp and argued forcefully, roused Xing's anger, and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Thousand-commander Lu Renqi, seeing no remedy, bowed to his father's portrait in court dress, stormed the camp to protest, and was killed in Su Xing's rage.

sentences.zh: 仁圻畜一犬，護屍不去，故吏梁玉收而葬之。

translations.literal: Renqi kept a dog that would not leave the corpse; former clerk Liang Yu recovered and buried him.
translations.idiomatic: Renqi's dog guarded the body; clerk Liang Yu gathered and buried him.

sentences.zh: 又廣安州知州徐盛、劍州知州向榮、商南縣知縣盧英、渠縣知縣王質、綦江縣知縣王無荒、營山縣知縣廖世正及典史劉廷臣、西安府知事張文選、司獄周勝驤、白水縣典史趙煥文，並以被脅不屈死。

translations.literal: Also Guang'an Prefecture Magistrate Xu Sheng; Jianzhou Magistrate Xiang Rong; Shangnan County Magistrate Lu Ying; Qu County Magistrate Wang Zhi; Qijiang County Magistrate Wang Wuhuang; Yingshan County Magistrate Liao Shizheng; and Archivist Liu Tingchen, Xi'an Prefecture Administrator Zhang Wenxuan, Prison Director Zhou Shengyang, and Baishui Archivist Zhao Huanwen—all died unyielding under coercion.
translations.idiomatic: Guang'an magistrate Xu Sheng, Jianzhou magistrate Xiang Rong, Shangnan magistrate Lu Ying, Qu magistrate Wang Zhi, Qijiang magistrate Wang Wuhuang, Yingshan magistrate Liao Shizheng, archivist Liu Tingchen, Xi'an administrator Zhang Wenxuan, prison director Zhou Shengyang, and Baishui archivist Zhao Huanwen likewise died rather than submit when pressed.

sentences.zh: 其以招諭死者：三桂未叛時，主事辛柱、筆帖式薩爾圖、隨侍郎哲爾肯★詔至滇。

translations.literal: Those who died on missions of persuasion: before Sangui rebelled, Director Xin Zhu, clerk Sartu, and Vice Minister Zhe'erken received the imperial charge to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Martyrs of persuasion: before the revolt Director Xin Zhu, clerk Sartu, and Vice Minister Zhe'erken bore the imperial message to Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 既叛，辛柱、薩爾圖將詣闕告變，賊殺之。

translations.literal: After the rebellion, Xin Zhu and Sartu were going to the capital to report the change; the rebels killed them.
translations.idiomatic: When Sangui rose Xin Zhu and Sartu set out to report; rebels killed them.

sentences.zh: 後則漢川巡檢章啟周，浙江會稽人。

translations.literal: Later there was Hanchuan Sub-Prefect Zhang Qizhou, a man of Kuaiji in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Later Hanchuan sub-prefect Zhang Qizhou of Zhejiang's Kuaiji died.

sentences.zh: 從順承郡王勒爾錦軍，以劄委通判往招諭三桂，被戕。

translations.literal: Following Prince of Shuncheng Jun Le'erjin's army, he was commissioned by dispatch as vice prefect to persuade Sangui and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: With Prince Le'erjin's army he was sent as vice prefect to summon Sangui and was slain.

sentences.zh: 及吳世璠時，又遣四品銜董重民往諭以順逆，至鎮遠，逆黨以弓弦縊殺之。

translations.literal: In Wu Shifan's time, they again sent Dong Chongmin with fourth-rank insignia to instruct on loyalty and treason; reaching Zhenyuan, rebel bands strangled him with bowstrings.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wu Shifan they sent fourth-rank Dong Chongmin to preach loyalty and treason; at Zhenyuan rebels garroted him.

sentences.zh: 又揚威大將軍簡親王喇布檄益陽縣知縣徐碭往衡州招撫三桂餘黨，至泉溪渡，為偽將軍吳國貴所殺。

translations.literal: Also General of Majestic Might Prince of Jian La Bu ordered Yiyang Magistrate Xu Yang to Hengzhou to pacify Sangui's remnant bands; at Quanxi Ford he was killed by the rebel general Wu Guogui.
translations.idiomatic: Prince La Bu of Jian sent Yiyang magistrate Xu Yang to pacify remnant rebels at Hengzhou; at Quanxi Ford the rebel Wu Guogui killed him.

sentences.zh: 鄖陽降調通判許文耀、阿迷州吏目郭維賢，亦均以招撫三桂餘黨遇害。

translations.literal: Yunyang demoted Vice Prefect Xu Wenyao and Ami Sub-Prefect Guo Weixian also met harm while pacifying Sangui's remnant bands.
translations.idiomatic: Demoted Yunyang vice prefect Xu Wenyao and Ami clerk Guo Weixian likewise died on pacification missions.

sentences.zh: 郎中祝表正隨經略大學士莫洛討叛鎮王輔臣，莫洛戰歿，輔臣幽表正於營，尋复具疏附表正還奏。

translations.literal: Director Zhu Biaozheng followed Grand Secretary and Commissioner-General Moluo to campaign against rebel commander Wang Fuchen; Moluo fell in battle; Fuchen detained Biaozheng in camp, then again prepared a memorial attached to Biaozheng to return and report.
translations.idiomatic: Director Zhu Biaozheng followed Commissioner-General Moluo against Wang Fuchen; Moluo fell; Fuchen held Biaozheng, then sent a memorial back with him.

sentences.zh: 聖祖即遣表正諭輔臣，至，則百方曉譬，留弗遣，卒為偽總兵巴三綱所殺。

translations.literal: The Sacred Ancestor then sent Biaozheng to instruct Fuchen; on arrival he admonished in every way but was detained and not released, and in the end was killed by the rebel commander Ba Sangang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Biaozheng to reason with Fuchen; he pleaded every way but was held; the rebel Ba Sangang killed him.

sentences.zh: 甘肅靜寧州知州王札亦以單騎諭輔臣禍福，被脅不屈，死。

translations.literal: Gansu Jingning Magistrate Wang Zha also went alone on horseback to instruct Fuchen on fortune and harm, was coerced and would not yield, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Jingning magistrate Wang Zha rode alone to warn Fuchen, was pressed to submit, refused, and died.

sentences.zh: 又撫叛鎮王屏籓死者，為四川鎮標副將徐升耀，劄付通判王官表、沈日章，劄付參將吳子騄等。

translations.literal: Those who died pacifying rebel commander Wang Pingfan included Sichuan Garrison Vice Commander Xu Shengyao; commissioned Vice Prefects Wang Guanbiao and Shen Rizhang; commissioned Vice Commander Wu Ziluan and others.
translations.idiomatic: Martyrs sent to pacify Wang Pingfan included Sichuan vice commander Xu Shengyao, commissioned vice prefects Wang Guanbiao and Shen Rizhang, and commissioned vice commander Wu Ziluan.

sentences.zh: 周岱生，字青岳，江西德化人。

translations.literal: Zhou Daisheng, style name Qingyue, was a man of Dehua in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Daisheng (Qingyue) came from Jiangxi's Dehua.

sentences.zh: 由拔貢生除貴州餘慶縣知縣，改廣西平南縣知縣。

translations.literal: From selected tribute student he was appointed magistrate of Yuyu County in Guizhou, then transferred to magistrate of Pingnan County in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Selected tribute student, he was Yuyu magistrate in Guizhou, then Pingnan magistrate in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，吳三桂叛，六月，其黨破梧州，攻平南，岱生練鄉團俍兵拒之大峽口，鏖戰三日，斬其魁。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, Wu Sangui rebelled; in the sixth month his bands took Wuzhou and attacked Pingnan; Daisheng trained militia and Liang troops to resist at Great Gorge Pass, fought fiercely three days, and beheaded their leader.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 13, when Sangui rebelled, his men took Wuzhou in the sixth month and struck Pingnan; Daisheng rallied militia and Liang auxiliaries at Great Gorge Pass, fought three days, and slew their chief.

sentences.zh: 七月，復大至，岱生奮身拒戰，攻益急，鄉團皆戰死，退保城。

translations.literal: In the seventh month they came again in force; Daisheng threw himself into the fight; the attack grew fiercer; the militia all died in battle, and he withdrew to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the rebels returned; Daisheng fought at the fore until every militiaman fell, then fell back behind the walls.

sentences.zh: 圍固援絕，自寅戰至午，城陷。

translations.literal: The siege tightened and aid was cut off; from the hour of Yin he fought until noon, and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Besieged without relief, he fought from dawn to noon until the city fell.

sentences.zh: 賊縶岱生往潯州，脅降，罵不絕口。

translations.literal: Rebels bound Daisheng and sent him to Xunzhou, coercing surrender; he cursed without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels bound him for Xunzhou to force his surrender; he cursed them without pause.

sentences.zh: 妻楊氏，於路先自剄死。

translations.literal: His wife, Lady Yang, first cut her throat on the road and died.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Yang cut her throat on the road before they arrived.

sentences.zh: 旋又甘言誘岱生降，卒遇害。

translations.literal: Soon they again used sweet words to entice Daisheng to submit; in the end he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: They tried flattery next; in the end they killed him.

sentences.zh: 長子儒且哭且{罒馬}，死尤慘。

translations.literal: His eldest son Ru wept as he was dragged along and died especially horribly.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Ru wept as he was hauled away and died in still greater agony.

sentences.zh: 岱生令餘慶時，有老賊陳四者，盤踞大同山垂三十年，剿捕不能得，出奇計招之，親至其巢，曉譬利害，曰：「王師且至，吾生汝！」

translations.literal: When Daisheng was magistrate of Yuyu, there was an old bandit Chen Si who had held Datong Mountain for nearly thirty years and could not be taken by pursuit; he devised a stratagem to summon him, went in person to the lair, and explained advantage and harm, saying: "The royal army is coming—I spare your life!"
translations.idiomatic: As Yuyu magistrate he faced Chen Si, who had held Datong Mountain thirty years despite repeated campaigns; Daisheng went alone to the lair and warned: "Imperial troops are coming—I spare you!

sentences.zh: 賊感泣，誓終其身無反。

translations.literal: The bandit was moved to tears and wept, swearing that for the rest of his life he would not rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The outlaw wept at his words and vowed never to turn against the dynasty again.

sentences.zh: 岱生曰：「盍隨我至縣城乎？」

translations.literal: Daisheng said: "Why not follow me to the county seat?"
translations.idiomatic: Dai Sheng asked, "Would you come with me to the county town?

sentences.zh: 賊諾之。

translations.literal: The bandit assented.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是至縣署，賜之食，厚為之裝而遣之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went to the county yamen, bestowed food upon him, richly equipped him, and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: He then brought him to the magistrate's office, fed him generously, fitted him out well, and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 其後吳逆之變，他縣賊皆響應，惟陳四不受偽職。

translations.literal: Afterward, at the uprising of the Wu rebel, bandits in other counties all responded; only Chen Four did not accept a false office.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui's rebellion broke out, outlaws in neighboring counties joined in—but Chen Si alone refused any rebel appointment.

sentences.zh: 平南市荒民少，岱生捐俸招集，始至，城內草屋九間。

translations.literal: Pingnan market was desolate and the people few; Daisheng donated his salary to gather them; when he first arrived, within the city were nine thatched huts.
translations.idiomatic: Pingnan was a wasteland with scarcely any inhabitants; Dai Sheng spent his own salary to draw people in, and when he first took office only nine grass huts stood inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 未幾，商民大集。

translations.literal: Before long, merchants and people gathered in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Within a short time merchants and townspeople flocked in.

sentences.zh: 俗窳不產蔬菜，岱生教以播種灌溉之方，畦畝鱗次相屬。

translations.literal: The custom was coarse and did not produce vegetables; Daisheng taught them methods of sowing and irrigation, and field plots lined up scale-like one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: Local habits were backward and vegetables scarcely grew; he taught planting and irrigation until garden beds stretched in orderly rows.

sentences.zh: 田皆老荒弗闢，又招粵東流民後先千餘家，報墾昇科，其他善政尤多。

translations.literal: The fields were all old waste land not opened; moreover he recruited more than a thousand households of Cantonese eastern migrants coming one after another, reported reclaiming and advanced tax quota, and his other good policies were especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He also brought in over a thousand Cantonese refugee families to open long-fallow land, registered the new farms for taxation, and enacted many other reforms besides.

sentences.zh: 楊三知，字知斯，直隸良鄉人。

translations.literal: Yang Sanzhi, courtesy name Zhisi, was a man of Liangxiang in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sanzhi (style name Zhisi) came from Liangxiang in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 順治三年進士，授山西榆次縣知縣。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the third year of Shunzhi, he was appointed magistrate of Yuci County in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Shunzhi year 3 and was made magistrate of Yuci in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 榆次經流賊殘破後，井裡蕭條，三知以恩義安輯，戶口日增。

translations.literal: After Yuci had been ravaged by roving bandits, wells and lanes were desolate; Sanzhi with grace and righteousness pacified and gathered them, and registered households daily increased.
translations.idiomatic: Yuci lay in ruins after years of roaming bandits; Yang governed with kindness and justice until the population steadily recovered.

sentences.zh: 康熙五年，大同鎮總兵姜瓖叛，連陷州縣，攻榆次。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kangxi, the Datong garrison commander-in-chief Jiang Xiang rebelled, successively capturing prefectures and counties, and attacked Yuci.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 5 the Datong commander Jiang Xiang rebelled, seized one district after another, and laid siege to Yuci.

sentences.zh: 三知勵吏民，募鄉勇守城。

translations.literal: Sanzhi exhorted clerks and people, recruited local braves to defend the city.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied officials and townsfolk and raised militia to hold the walls.

sentences.zh: 夜遣人斫賊營，間有斬獲，賊不退。

translations.literal: At night he sent men to cut at the rebel camp; occasionally there were beheadings and captures, but the rebels did not withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: He sent night raiders against the rebel encampments and won minor victories, yet the enemy would not lift the siege.

sentences.zh: 三知令偃旗鼓，示弱。

translations.literal: Sanzhi ordered drums and banners lowered, showing weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Yang ordered the drums and banners stilled to feign weakness.

sentences.zh: 賊徑薄城，攀堞欲登，三知急起，麾眾發矢石，斃甚眾。

translations.literal: The rebels pressed straight against the city, climbed the parapets intending to mount; Sanzhi rose in haste, directed the multitude to release arrows and stones, and killed very many.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels rushed the walls and scrambled up the battlements; Yang sprang to the ramparts and had his men pour down arrows and stones, killing large numbers.

sentences.zh: 賊憤，益兵圍之。

translations.literal: The rebels were furious and increased troops to besiege it.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, they brought up reinforcements and tightened the encirclement.

sentences.zh: 相持逾六月，敬謹親王尼堪分兵來援，賊始敗走。

translations.literal: They faced off for more than six months; the Prince Jingjin Nikan divided troops to come in relief, and the rebels at last were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The standoff lasted more than half a year until Prince Jingjin Nikan arrived with relief troops and drove the rebels away.

sentences.zh: 三知設保甲、練屯聚，复捐俸、立社學，置膳田以資膏火，士民感之。

translations.literal: Sanzhi established baojia, drilled tuntun clusters, again donated salary, founded a community school, set up kitchen fields to supply lamp oil and fire, and scholars and people were grateful.
translations.idiomatic: He organized local militia, drilled garrison communities, again donated his salary to found a village school and endow grain lands for students' expenses—the people were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 擢兵部主事，累遷郎中，外擢四川松龍道、上東道。

translations.literal: He was promoted to a principal clerk in the Ministry of War, repeatedly transferred to langzhong, and outwardly promoted to Songlong Circuit in Sichuan and Shangdong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted within the Ministry of War to department director, he was later posted to the Songlong and Shangdong circuits in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 上東道屬經張獻忠慘戮，存者在絕峒密箐中，招徠千數百家，築堡渝東，民名之曰楊公堡。

translations.literal: Shangdong Circuit's subprefectures had been horribly slaughtered by Zhang Xianzhong; survivors were in remote gorges and dense bamboo ravines; he recruited more than a thousand households, built a fort east of Yu, and the people named it Lord Yang's Fort.
translations.idiomatic: The region had been devastated by Zhang Xianzhong's massacres, with survivors hiding in remote valleys; he drew back more than a thousand families and built a fort east of Chongqing that the people called Yang's Fort.

sentences.zh: 十一年，補陝西神木道。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he was transferred to fill Shenmu Circuit in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 he was appointed to the Shenmu circuit in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 十三年，入覲，還至保德，聞提督王輔臣叛附吳三桂，從者勸遲行，勿渡河，不聽，疾馳還署，圖城守。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he entered court audience; returning to Baode, he heard Governor Wang Fuchen had rebelled and attached to Wu Sangui; followers advised delaying travel and not crossing the river—he did not listen, sped back to his yamen, and planned city defense.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13, while returning from an audience at court, he reached Baode and learned that Governor Wang Fuchen had defected to Wu Sangui; his escort urged him to wait and not cross the Yellow River, but he refused, galloped back to his post, and prepared to defend the city.

sentences.zh: 曩三桂剿闖賊殘孽，過神木，市恩，民謬德之，立生祠，三知即毀之。

translations.literal: Formerly Sangui had suppressed remnant bandits of the roving rebels, passed through Shenmu, traded favors; the people wrongly felt grateful and erected a living shrine; Sanzhi immediately destroyed it.
translations.idiomatic: Years earlier Wu Sangui had passed through Shenmu while hunting rebel remnants and curried favor with the people, who mistakenly built him a shrine of living worship—Yang promptly tore it down.

sentences.zh: 察知縣孫世譽忠實可倚，時輔臣播偽劄，將弁多為所誘，分據城堡，惟韓城知縣翟世琪與神木通聲援。

translations.literal: He observed that Magistrate Sun Shiyu was loyal and could be relied upon; at the time Fuchen spread false commissions, and officers and commanders mostly were enticed by him, each holding castles separately; only Hancheng Magistrate Zhai Shiqi and Shenmu communicated mutual reinforcement.
translations.idiomatic: He found the county magistrate Sun Shiyu trustworthy; Wang Fuchen was circulating forged commissions and winning over many officers who seized forts across the region—only Zhai Shiqi of Hancheng remained in contact with Shenmu for mutual support.

sentences.zh: 世譽，隸鑲紅旗；

translations.literal: Shiyu belonged to the Bordered Red Banner;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shiyu was a bondsman of the Bordered Red Banner;

sentences.zh: 世琪，山東益都人，順治十六年進士：關中並稱賢令者也。

translations.literal: Shiqi, a man of Yidu in Shandong, jinshi in the sixteenth year of Shunzhi: together in Guanzhong they were called worthy magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Shiqi, a Shunzhi-16 jinshi from Yidu in Shandong—together they were known as the worthy magistrates of the Guanzhong region.

sentences.zh: 叛黨朱龍犯神木，民恟懼。

translations.literal: Rebel faction Zhu Long invaded Shenmu; the people were alarmed and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Zhu Long attacked Shenmu, throwing the populace into panic.

sentences.zh: 三知適受檄赴京師代賀，有諷可攜眷行者，謝之。

translations.literal: Sanzhi happened to receive orders to go to the capital to offer congratulations in proxy; some subtly suggested he could take dependents on the journey—he declined.
translations.idiomatic: Yang had just received orders to go to the capital on congratulatory business; some hinted he should take his family along, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 赴闕事竣，抵署三日，延安、吳堡相繼陷。

translations.literal: After finishing business at court, three days after reaching his yamen, Yan'an and Wubu fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He completed his mission and returned to his post; within three days Yan'an and Wubu had both fallen.

sentences.zh: 賊至，乘城死守，親挽強弩，發無不中。

translations.literal: When rebels arrived, he mounted the wall and defended unto death, personally drawing powerful crossbows, and every shot hit.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels came he manned the walls in a last stand, personally drawing heavy crossbows—every bolt found its mark.

sentences.zh: 柳溝營游擊李師膺受偽劄，鼓眾譟餉，世琪出諭賊，先被戕，及其二子。

translations.literal: Liugou Camp guerrilla colonel Li Shiying received a false commission, roused the crowd clamoring for pay; Shiqi went out to admonish the rebels and was first killed, along with his two sons.
translations.idiomatic: Guerrilla colonel Li Shiying of Liugou Camp accepted a forged commission and stirred the troops to riot for pay; Zhai Shiqi went out to reason with the mutineers and was murdered first, together with his two sons.

sentences.zh: 神木守將孫崇雅亦通賊，城遂陷。

translations.literal: Shenmu garrison commander Sun Chongya also communicated with rebels, and the city then fell.
translations.idiomatic: The Shenmu garrison commander Sun Chongya also colluded with the rebels, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 崇雅合賊將環說三知，以延綏開府啗之，不應；

translations.literal: Chongya united with rebel generals surrounding and persuading Sanzhi, using an open-office post in Yan'an and Sui to entice him—he did not respond;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chongya and rebel generals surrounded Yang and tried to lure him with the governorship of Yan-Sui—he refused.

sentences.zh: 脅交敕印，不與；

translations.literal: They coerced him to hand over the commission and seal—he did not give them;
translations.idiomatic: They demanded his commission and seal—he would not yield them.

sentences.zh: 賊迭以甘言誘三知，且擁回署，三知過井，厲聲諭家人勿作兒女態，躍而入，賊遽縋出之，臂已折。

translations.literal: Rebels repeatedly used sweet words to entice Sanzhi, and moreover escorted him back to the yamen; Sanzhi passed a well, sternly admonished family not to act in childish manner, leaped in; rebels hurriedly hauled him out, and his arm was already broken.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sweet-talked him and hustled him back to his residence; passing the well he loudly told his household not to weep like cowards and sprang in—the rebels hastily hauled him out with his arm already broken.

sentences.zh: 力以三知「在官廉平，初未相迫，毋自苦」為詞，三知大罵不絕口，乃舁置別室，環守之，載脅載誘。

translations.literal: Li earnestly used as words to Sanzhi, "In office you were honest and fair, at first we did not press you—do not torment yourself"; Sanzhi cursed loudly without pause; thereupon they carried him to a separate room, encircled and guarded him, alternately threatening and enticing.
translations.idiomatic: Li urged that Yang had always been upright and they had not meant to harm him, pleading that he spare himself—but Yang cursed them without cease, so they moved him to another room, kept guards around him, and alternated threats with blandishments.

sentences.zh: 一夕，忽合扉，不知何以賊之。

translations.literal: One night, suddenly the doors were closed shut; it was not known how he had perished at the rebels' hands.
translations.idiomatic: One night the doors swung shut suddenly; no one outside knew how he had died among the rebels.

sentences.zh: 其妻妾及二女俱赴井以殉。

translations.literal: His wife, concubines, and two daughters all went to the well to die as martyrs.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, concubines, and two daughters all threw themselves into the well in martyrdom.

sentences.zh: 城復後，家人始於淺土中獲三知遺骸，經長夏，面色如生。

translations.literal: After the city was recovered, the family only then obtained Sanzhi's remaining bones from shallow earth; having passed the long summer, his face color was as if alive.
translations.idiomatic: After the city was retaken his family recovered Yang's remains from a shallow grave; though a full summer had passed, his face looked as though he still lived.

sentences.zh: 世譽亦抗節不屈，賊羈之深室，輔臣後降，卒害世譽以滅口。

translations.literal: Shiyu also resisted principle and did not submit; rebels detained him in a deep chamber; after Fuchen later surrendered, they at last harmed Shiyu to silence mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shiyu likewise held out and refused to yield; the rebels held him in a sealed room; after Wang Fuchen eventually surrendered, they killed Sun to silence him.

sentences.zh: 劉嘉猷，字憲明，江西金溪人。

translations.literal: Liu Jiayou, courtesy name Xianming, was a man of Jinxi in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jiayou (style name Xianming) was a native of Jinxi in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 由明舉人順治初署興國、新建教諭，以正誼明道為教，士多化之。

translations.literal: From Ming-era provincial graduate, in early Shunzhi he acted as instructor in Xingguo and Xinjian, taking upright principle and illuminating the Way as teaching, and many scholars were transformed.
translations.idiomatic: A Ming-era provincial graduate, he served early in Shunzhi as instructor in Xingguo and Xinjian, teaching moral principle until his students were deeply changed.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，改福建侯官縣知縣，為閩浙總督范承謨所賞。

translations.literal: When his term ended, he was changed to magistrate of Houguan County in Fujian, and was appreciated by Fujian-Zhejiang Governor-General Fan Chengmou.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he was appointed magistrate of Houguan in Fujian and won the esteem of Governor-General Fan Chengmou.

sentences.zh: 撤籓命下，嘉猷度平南王耿精忠必應吳三桂叛，謂家人以「既宰茲土，義不汙賊」。

translations.literal: When the order to abolish feudatories was issued, Jiayou judged that Pingnan Prince Geng Jingzhong would surely follow Wu Sangui in rebellion, and told his family, "Having governed this land, righteousness does not permit staining oneself with rebels."
translations.idiomatic: When the order to abolish the feudatories came down, Liu foresaw that Prince Pingnan Geng Jingzhong would join Wu Sangui's revolt and told his household, "Having ruled this soil, I cannot dishonor myself by serving rebels."

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年三月，精忠紿文武赴籓府計事，嘉猷從承謨後。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirteenth year of Kangxi, Jingzhong deceived civil and military officials to come to the princely mansion to plan affairs; Jiayou followed behind Chengmou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Kangxi 13, Geng Jingzhong summoned Fujian's officials to his palace on pretense of consultation; Liu Jiayou went with Fan Chengmou.

sentences.zh: 見鋒刃交戟脅承謨降，不屈，縛以去，嘉猷歷階而上，厲聲叱精忠，福州府知府王之儀、建寧府同知喻三畏同發憤罵賊。

translations.literal: Seeing blades crossed and halberds threatening Chengmou to submit, he did not yield; they bound him and took him away; Jiayou ascended the steps, sternly rebuked Jingzhong; Fuzhou Prefect Wang Zhiyi and Jianning Assistant Prefect Yu Sanwei together in anger cursed the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When armed men surrounded Fan Chengmou and demanded his surrender, he refused and was seized; Liu strode up the steps and denounced Geng Jingzhong, while Prefect Wang Zhiyi and Assistant Prefect Yu Sanwei cursed the rebels in fury.

sentences.zh: 精忠喝武士殺三人，眾股栗。

translations.literal: Jingzhong shouted for warriors to kill the three men; the crowd's thighs trembled.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Jingzhong ordered his guards to execute the three men, and the assembly trembled with fear.

sentences.zh: 嘉猷戟手作搏擊勢，芒刃亟下，與之儀、三畏同時被害。

translations.literal: Jiayou pointed with his halberd-hand in a grappling posture; sharp blades swiftly descended, and together with Zhiyi and Sanwei he was harmed at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: Liu raised his hands as if to fight; the blades fell at once, and he died together with Wang Zhiyi and Yu Sanwei.

sentences.zh: 城守千總廖有功見逆殺三人，發憤大呼，亦死之。

translations.literal: Garrison thousand-commander Liao Yougong saw the rebels kill the three men, cried out in indignant rage, and also died.
translations.idiomatic: Thousand-commander Liao Yougong, seeing the rebels murder the three officials, shouted in outrage and was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 高天爵，字君寵，漢軍鑲白旗人，後改隸鑲黃旗。

translations.literal: Gao Tianjue, courtesy name Junchong, was a man of the Bordered White Banner of the Han Army, later changed to belong to the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Tianjue (style name Junchong), originally of the Han Bordered White Banner, was later reassigned to the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 由廕生於順治四年任山東高苑縣知縣，累官至江西建昌府知府。

translations.literal: Through yinsheng in the fourth year of Shunzhi he served as magistrate of Gaoyuan County in Shandong, and by accumulated offices reached prefect of Jianchang Prefecture in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Entering service by hereditary privilege in Shunzhi 4 as magistrate of Gaoyuan in Shandong, he rose through the ranks to prefect of Jianchang in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 先是廣昌山賊踞羊石、滴水二砦為巢穴，官軍仰攻，輒為滾木礧石所傷，罷攻，招降，賊佯就撫，仍伺隙煽亂。

translations.literal: Earlier, Guangchang mountain bandits occupied Yangshi and Dishui two stockades as nests; government troops attacked from below, and were always wounded by rolling logs and piled stones, so attacks ceased; they recruited surrender, and bandits pretended to accept pacification yet still watched for openings to incite disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits in the hills of Guangchang had long held fortresses at Yangshi and Dishui; government troops storming uphill were cut down by rolling logs and rocks, so the siege was abandoned and amnesty offered—the bandits feigned submission while waiting to stir trouble again.

sentences.zh: 官軍斃之獄，餘賊益負固。

translations.literal: Government troops put them to death in prison; the remaining bandits became more obstinate in defense.
translations.idiomatic: When officials executed captured bandits in prison, the survivors grew only more defiant.

sentences.zh: 適風雨交作，漂流樹木，衝斷橋梁，賊保巢不出。

translations.literal: Just then wind and rain came together, floating and drifting trees, rushing and breaking bridges; bandits guarded the nest and did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: A storm then washed uprooted trees downstream and wrecked the bridges, trapping the bandits in their stronghold.

sentences.zh: 天爵會巡道參將出不意直搗之，擒斬，盡毀其巢。

translations.literal: Tianjue joined the circuit intendant and regional commander in an unexpected straight thrust, captured and beheaded them, and completely destroyed their nests.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Tianjue joined the circuit intendant and a regional commander in a surprise assault, captured and executed the leaders, and razed their lairs completely.

sentences.zh: 耿精忠據閩叛，縱黨入江西，犯建昌，時天爵已擢兩淮鹽運使，或勸之速行，天爵以「守此土十六年，雖受代，不可遽離」答之，率家丁數十人禦賊萬年橋。

translations.literal: Geng Jingzhong held Fujian in rebellion and let his faction enter Jiangxi, invading Jianchang; at the time Tianjue had already been promoted to Liang-Huai salt transport commissioner; some urged him to travel quickly; Tianjue answered with "Having guarded this soil sixteen years, though having received replacement, one cannot abruptly leave," led several dozen household retainers to resist rebels at Wannian Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled and sent troops into Jiangxi against Jianchang, Gao had already been promoted to salt commissioner of Liang-Huai; advisers urged him to flee, but he replied, "I have governed this land for sixteen years—even though my successor has arrived, I cannot abandon it now," and led a few dozen retainers to hold Wannian Bridge against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 城守副將趙印已降賊，乘天爵力戰，從後縛之，獻賊，載送入閩，再四誘降，不屈，囚之。

translations.literal: Deputy garrison commander Zhao Yin had already surrendered to rebels; while Tianjue fought with strength, from behind he bound him, presented him to rebels, and sent him into Fujian; again and again they enticed him to submit, he did not yield, and they imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commander Zhao Yin had already defected; while Gao fought fiercely, Zhao seized him from behind and handed him to the rebels, who sent him into Fujian; they tried repeatedly to win him over, but he refused and was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 越歲餘，與副將王進，武舉胡守謙，把總楊起鵬、薑山等同謀，遣千總徐得功出仙霞嶺迎大軍入關，陰結死士為內應。

translations.literal: After more than a year, together with deputy commander Wang Jin, military graduate Hu Shouqian, platoon commanders Yang Qipeng, Jiang Shan, and others he plotted, sent thousand-commander Xu Degong out Xianxia Ridge to welcome the great army entering the pass, and secretly joined dead-loyal men as inner responders.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he conspired with Deputy Commander Wang Jin, military graduate Hu Shouqian, and platoon commanders Yang Qipeng and Jiang Shan, sending Thousand-Commander Xu Degong through Xianxia Pass to guide imperial troops into Fujian while loyalists inside prepared to rise.

sentences.zh: 賊黨偵而訐之，十五年九月四日遇害。

translations.literal: Rebel faction spied and exposed it; on the fourth day of the ninth month of the fifteenth year he met with harm.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel agents discovered the plot, and on the fourth day of the ninth month in year 15 he was murdered.

sentences.zh: 後以福建巡撫卞永譽請，以天爵與原任福寧總兵吳萬福、福州府知府王之儀、邵武府知府張瑞午、建寧府同知喻三畏、邵武府同知高舉、侯官縣知縣劉嘉猷、尤溪縣知縣李員、福州城守千總廖有功等合建一祠於省城西門外，復以子其佩請扁，書「藎忱義烈」四字以額其家祠。

translations.literal: Afterward, at Fujian Governor Bian Yongyu's request, Tianjue together with former Funing commander Wu Wanfu, Fuzhou Prefect Wang Zhiyi, Shaowu Prefect Zhang Ruwu, Jianning Assistant Prefect Yu Sanwei, Shaowu Assistant Prefect Gao Ju, Houguan Magistrate Liu Jiayou, Youxi Magistrate Li Yuan, Fuzhou garrison thousand-commander Liao Yougong, and others jointly built one shrine outside the provincial west gate; again at his son Qi Pei's request for a plaque, wrote the four characters "Loyal Devotion, Righteous Fervor" to title their family shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at the request of Fujian governor Bian Yongyu, a joint shrine was built outside the west gate of the provincial capital for Gao Tianjue, former Funing commander Wu Wanfu, Wang Zhiyi, Zhang Ruwu, Yu Sanwei, Gao Ju, Liu Jiayou, Li Yuan, Liao Yougong, and others; Gao's son Qi Pei also obtained an imperial inscription of four characters—"Steadfast Loyalty, Righteous Valor"—for the family memorial hall.

sentences.zh: 長子其位自有傳。

translations.literal: The eldest son Qiwei has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Qiwei has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 李成功，奉天鐵嶺人。

translations.literal: Li Chenggong, a man of Tieling in Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chenggong was a native of Tieling in Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 順治六年武進士。

translations.literal: A military jinshi in the sixth year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He took second place in the military metropolitan examination in Shunzhi 6.

sentences.zh: 歷官至廣東潮州參將。

translations.literal: By accumulated offices he reached Guangdong Chaozhou regional vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to vice commander of Chaozhou in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，總兵劉進忠應耿精忠叛。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, Commander Liu Jinzhong responded to Geng Jingzhong in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 13 regional commander Liu Jinzhong joined Geng Jingzhong's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 成功潛與游擊張善繼等謀誅進忠，事覺，進忠以兵脅同叛，曰：「汝為我中軍，我視汝猶子，何無義至此？」

translations.literal: Chenggong secretly with guerrilla colonel Zhang Shanji and others plotted to kill Jinzhong; the matter was discovered; Jinzhong with troops coerced him to rebel together, saying: "You serve as my central army; I regard you as a son—how without righteousness to this extent?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Chenggong secretly plotted with guerrilla colonel Zhang Shanji and others to assassinate Liu Jinzhong, but the plot was discovered; Jinzhong surrounded him with troops and pressed him to rebel, saying, "You are my chief of staff—I treat you like a son. How can you be so faithless?"

sentences.zh: 成功曰：「祿山叛國，死於豬兒；

translations.literal: Chenggong said: "Lushan rebelled against the state and died at the hands of Zhuer;
translations.idiomatic: Li replied, "An Lushan betrayed the empire and was killed by his own son;

sentences.zh: 朱泚叛國，死於韓旻；

translations.literal: Zhu Ci rebelled against the state and died at the hands of Han Min;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci betrayed the empire and was slain by Han Min;

sentences.zh: 汝今叛國，不知死之將至！

translations.literal: you now rebel against the state—do you not know death is about to arrive!
translations.idiomatic: you now betray the throne—do you not see your end is near!

sentences.zh: 我何為從汝？」

translations.literal: I—why should I act as one who follows you?"
translations.idiomatic: Why should I follow you?"

sentences.zh: 進忠命斬之，罵不絕口而死。

translations.literal: Jinzhong ordered him beheaded; he cursed without pause unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong ordered him executed; he cursed without stopping until he died.

sentences.zh: 善繼，直隸彭城衛人。

translations.literal: Shanji, a man of Pengcheng Guard in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shanji came from Pengcheng Guard in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 習儒，通孫吳兵法。

translations.literal: He studied Confucian learning and mastered Sun and Wu's military methods.
translations.idiomatic: Trained in the classics, he mastered the arts of war taught by Sunzi and Wuzi.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年第二名武進士，授潮州城守營游擊。

translations.literal: Second-place military jinshi in the sixth year of Kangxi, appointed Chaozhou city-garrison guerrilla colonel.
translations.idiomatic: Second in the military metropolitan examination in Kangxi 6, he was appointed guerrilla colonel of the Chaozhou city garrison.

sentences.zh: 進忠陰遣腹弁赴精忠獻款，弁歸，與進忠謀曰：「善繼剛方固執，深得眾心，宜亟散其卒。」

translations.literal: Jinzhong secretly sent a trusted lieutenant to Jingzhong to offer allegiance; the lieutenant returned and with Jinzhong plotted, saying: "Shanji is upright and obstinate, deeply winning the hearts of the multitude—one ought quickly to disperse his soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong secretly sent a trusted officer to Geng Jingzhong to pledge allegiance; on his return the officer told Jinzhong, "Zhang Shanji is rigid and upright and holds the troops' loyalty—you should disband his men at once."

sentences.zh: 進忠遂令所部分隸私黨。

translations.literal: Jinzhong thereupon ordered his division partly subordinated to private cliques.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jinzhong then reassigned his troops to his own partisans.

sentences.zh: 善繼麾下虛無人，謁進忠曰：「公不聞晉王敦乎？

translations.literal: Shanji's command was empty of men; he called on Jinzhong, saying: "Sir, have you not heard of Jin prince Wang Dun?
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of his soldiers, Zhang Shanji confronted Jinzhong: "Have you never heard of the Jin rebel Wang Dun?

sentences.zh: 威勢未嘗不赫也，兵敗身死，發瘞斬屍，未有叛國而克全終者！」

translations.literal: His might was never not brilliant, yet when troops were defeated his body died, the coffin was dug up and the corpse beheaded—never has one who rebelled against the state been able to preserve a whole end!"
translations.idiomatic: His power seemed invincible, yet when his army was broken he died, his grave opened and his corpse hacked apart—no traitor has ever escaped ruin!"

sentences.zh: 進忠怒，羈之馬王廟，貢生林應璧同被羈，日談古忠孝事。

translations.literal: Jinzhong was angry, detained him at Mawang Temple; licentiate Lin Yingbi was likewise detained, daily discussing ancient loyalty and filial piety matters.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Jinzhong imprisoned him at Mawang Temple together with licentiate Lin Yingbi; day after day they spoke of loyalty and filial piety in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 進忠屢遣人諭降，終不屈，令斬之。

translations.literal: Jinzhong repeatedly sent men to admonish him to submit; in the end he did not yield, and ordered him beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong sent envoys again and again to win him over, but he never yielded and was finally ordered executed.

sentences.zh: 白虎，陝西秦州人。

translations.literal: Bai Hu, a man of Qinzhou in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Hu was a native of Qinzhou in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙十一年，官澄海協右營都司，有「虎將」名。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Kangxi, he served as colonel of the right battalion of Chenghai Cooperative, and had the name "Tiger General."
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 11 he served as colonel of the right battalion of the Chenghai cooperative brigade and was known as the "Tiger General."

sentences.zh: 進忠將叛，調虎與其子崇質入郡。

translations.literal: Jinzhong was about to rebel and summoned Tiger together with his son Chongzhi into the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As Jinzhong prepared to rebel he summoned Bai Hu and his son Chongzhi to the prefectural city.

sentences.zh: 至，則知進忠有異志，★M4焉涕下。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he then knew Jinzhong had ulterior motives; upon hearing it, tears streamed down.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he saw that Jinzhong harbored treacherous designs; when he learned of it, tears streamed down his face.

sentences.zh: 進忠令虎易帽，虎曰：「頭可斷，帽不可易！」

translations.literal: Jinzhong ordered Tiger to change his hat; Tiger said: "The head may be cut off, but the hat may not be changed!"
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong ordered Bai Hu to switch to a rebel's cap; Bai Hu said, "You may take my head, but you will not change my hat!"

sentences.zh: 令翦辮，虎曰：「頸可截，辮不可翦！」

translations.literal: He ordered his queue cut; Tiger said: "The neck may be severed, but the queue may not be cut!"
translations.idiomatic: When told to cut off his queue, he said, "You may sever my neck, but you will not cut my queue!"

sentences.zh: 且責進忠，詞甚厲。

translations.literal: Moreover he reproached Jinzhong, his words very stern.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuked Jinzhong in the harshest terms.

sentences.zh: 左右以搖惑軍心，慫進忠斃之。

translations.literal: Those at his sides, on grounds of shaking and confusing army hearts, urged Jinzhong to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants, claiming he was demoralizing the troops, urged Jinzhong to put him to death.

sentences.zh: 進忠愛其勇，不忍，曰：「此愚人，不識時務耳！」

translations.literal: Jinzhong loved his bravery and could not bear it, saying: "This is a foolish man who does not know the times!"
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong admired his valor and could not bear to kill him, saying, "This fool does not understand the times!"

sentences.zh: 遂羈之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he detained him.
translations.idiomatic: He had him imprisoned instead.

sentences.zh: 篡取虎妻張、虎孫士俊為質。

translations.literal: Usurping and taking Tiger's wife Zhang and Tiger's grandson Shijun as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Bai Hu's wife, née Zhang, and his grandson Shijun as hostages.

sentences.zh: 虎與同志密遣人赴省請兵，約內應。

translations.literal: Tiger with comrades secretly sent men to the province to request troops, arranging an inner response.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Hu and his allies secretly sent messengers to the provincial capital to request troops and arrange an inside rising.

sentences.zh: 謀洩，將就刃，謂崇質曰：「死，吾分也！

translations.literal: The plot leaked; about to face the blade, he told Chongzhi: "Death is my portion!
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed and he faced execution, he told Chongzhi, "Death is my lot!

sentences.zh: 委身存祀則在汝。」

translations.literal: Entrusting the body to preserve sacrifices lies with you."
translations.idiomatic: It is for you to preserve our line and our rites."

sentences.zh: 崇質對曰：「父為忠臣，子從叛賊，烏乎可？」

translations.literal: Chongzhi replied: "Father is a loyal minister; the son follows rebel bandits—how can it be?"
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi answered, "If my father is a loyal minister, how can his son follow a rebel?"

sentences.zh: 縛至西市，虎望北叩首，大言曰：「君臣大義盡於此，父子至情，亦盡於此矣！」

translations.literal: Bound to the west market, Tiger looked north and knocked his head, speaking loudly: "The great righteousness of ruler and minister is exhausted here; father-son utmost feeling is also exhausted here!"
translations.idiomatic: Tied and led to the west market, Bai Hu kowtowed toward the north and declared, "Between sovereign and subject, duty ends here; between father and son, love ends here as well!"

sentences.zh: 觀者皆泣下。

translations.literal: The onlookers all wept and shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Every witness wept.

sentences.zh: 何亮，潮州人。

translations.literal: He Liang, a man of Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Liang was a native of Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 官澄海協千總。

translations.literal: He held office as a garrison company commander at Chenghai in the coastal defense command.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a company commander in the Chenghai coastal garrison.

sentences.zh: 虎以心腹待之，亮隨虎赴郡，進忠羈虎，旋以內應事泄，並將斬亮。

translations.literal: Hu treated him as heart-and-belly; Liang followed Hu to the prefectural city; Jinzhong detained Hu; soon the inside-collaborator affair leaked, and he was also about to execute Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Hu counted him among his inner circle, and Liang went with him to the prefectural seat. When Jinzhong seized Hu and the plot for internal collaboration was exposed, Liang was marked for execution as well.

sentences.zh: 進忠叱之，亮謂當訴於天，同時遇害。

translations.literal: Jinzhong shouted at him; Liang said one ought to appeal to Heaven; at the same time they met with harm and died.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong shouted him down, but Liang declared that his case belonged before Heaven. They were killed together.

sentences.zh: 其兄弟妻子被殺者尤眾。

translations.literal: Of his brothers, wives, and children, those who were killed were especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Even more of his brothers, wives, and children were put to the sword.

sentences.zh: 於國璉，奉天人。

translations.literal: Yu Guolian, a man of Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Guolian was a native of Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 為續順公沈瑞旗員。

translations.literal: He was a bannerman under the Continued-Submission Duke Shen Rui.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a banner soldier under Shen Rui, Duke of Continued Submission.

sentences.zh: 進忠亂作，瑞命偕都統宋文科、鄧光明攻之。

translations.literal: When Jinzhong's rebellion arose, Rui ordered that together with commandants Song Wenkē and Deng Guangming they attack him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinzhong rose in revolt, Shen Rui ordered Yu to join commandants Song Wenkē and Deng Guangming in attacking him.

sentences.zh: 戰太平街，三日，國璉身先士卒，射傷進忠左臂，賊披靡，以眾寡不敵，終為所敗。

translations.literal: They fought at Taiping Street for three days; Guolian's body went before soldiers, shot and wounded Jinzhong's left arm, the rebels scattered, but because few could not match many, in the end they were defeated by him.
translations.idiomatic: For three days they battled in Taiping Street. Guolian fought at the forefront, wounding Jinzhong's left arm and driving the rebels into flight, but sheer numbers told, and they were finally overrun.

sentences.zh: 瑞縛光明及國璉以降，國璉獨不屈，斬於市，屍僵立不僕，數日面如生，眾咸異之。

translations.literal: Rui bound Guangming and Guolian to submit in surrender; Guolian alone would not yield, was beheaded in the market, the corpse stiffened standing and did not fall, for several days the face was as in life, the crowd all regarded it as strange.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Rui bound Deng Guangming and Yu Guolian and offered them up in surrender. Yu alone refused to bend. Executed in the marketplace, his corpse remained rigid and upright without toppling. Days later his face still looked lifelike, and the people marveled.

sentences.zh: 嵇永仁，字留山，江南無錫人。

translations.literal: Ji Yongren, style name Liushan, a man of Wuxi in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Yongren, courtesy name Liushan, was from Wuxi in the lower Yangtze region.

sentences.zh: 用長洲籍入學為諸生。

translations.literal: Using the Changzhou register he entered study and became a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He enrolled through a Changzhou household registration and became a licensed scholar.

sentences.zh: 入閩浙總督范承謨幕。

translations.literal: He entered the staff of Fan Chengmo, governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the secretariat of Fan Chengmo, Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 耿精忠應吳三桂叛，執承謨，脅永仁與同幕王龍光、沈天成及承謨族弟承譜降，不從，被執。

translations.literal: Geng Jingzhong responded to Wu Sangui's rebellion, seized Chengmo, compelled Yongren and fellow staff members Wang Longguang, Shen Tiancheng, and Chengmo's clansman younger brother Chengpu to surrender; they did not comply and were seized.
translations.idiomatic: When Geng Jingzhong threw in with Wu Sangui's revolt, he took Fan Chengmo prisoner and tried to force Yongren, his colleagues Wang Longguang and Shen Tiancheng, and Fan's kinsman Chengpu to submit. They refused and were arrested.

sentences.zh: 永仁少好從士大夫遊，討論國家典故，六曹章奏，條分件系，著有集政備考一書。

translations.literal: From youth Yongren enjoyed following scholar-officials in travel, discussing state precedents and the six ministries' memorials, dividing them item by item into categories; he wrote one book, Collected Administration Reference.
translations.idiomatic: From his youth he kept company with scholar-officials, debating state precedents and the memorials of the six ministries with meticulous order. He authored Collected Administration Reference.

sentences.zh: 以範、嵇世交，故相從至閩。

translations.literal: Because the Fan and Ji families were friends across generations, therefore he followed to Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: The Fan and Ji families had been friends for generations, so he accompanied Fan to Fujian.

sentences.zh: 時精忠蓄謀未發，屢陳弭變策，如請撥協餉、補綠旗兵、安插逃弁、條議屯田諸端，冀固民心、殺賊勢。

translations.literal: At that time Jingzhong's plot had not yet been launched; he repeatedly presented plans to quell the crisis, such as requesting allotment of auxiliary pay, supplementing Green Standard troops, resettling fugitive officers, and proposing garrison-field measures on many points, hoping to solidify popular hearts and diminish rebel momentum.
translations.idiomatic: While Jingzhong's conspiracy was still ripening, he repeatedly urged measures to forestall rebellion—allocating auxiliary funds, replenishing Green Standard forces, resettling deserters, and drafting garrison-field proposals—all aimed at steadying the people and blunting the rebels' strength.

sentences.zh: 又請借巡視沿海為名，提輕兵駐上游制賊。

translations.literal: He also requested, under the pretext of touring and inspecting the coast, to lead light troops stationed upstream to restrain the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He further asked leave to patrol the coast in name only, while leading a light force upstream to pin the rebels down.

sentences.zh: 以文武吏皆預中賊餌，號令格不行。

translations.literal: Because civil and military officials all beforehand had taken the rebels' bait, orders encountered obstruction and would not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: But civil and military officers had already been bought off, so his orders were blocked at every turn.

sentences.zh: 在獄凡三年，賊害承謨，乃痛哭自經死。

translations.literal: In prison altogether three years; when the rebels killed Chengmo, then he wept bitterly and hanged himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: He remained in prison three years. When the rebels murdered Fan Chengmo, he wept and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 永仁知醫，著有東田醫補。

translations.literal: Yongren knew medicine and wrote Eastern Field Medical Supplement.
translations.idiomatic: He was versed in medicine and wrote Eastern Field Medical Supplement.

sentences.zh: 工詩詞，有竹林集、葭林堂詩。

translations.literal: He was skilled at poetry and lyrics; he had Bamboo Grove Collection and Jialin Hall Poems.
translations.idiomatic: He was an accomplished poet, leaving Bamboo Grove Collection and Jialin Hall Poems.

sentences.zh: 獄中又著詩二卷、文一卷。

translations.literal: In prison he again wrote two juan of poetry and one juan of prose.
translations.idiomatic: While imprisoned he also composed two scrolls of verse and one of prose.

sentences.zh: 與龍光相倡和者，又有百苦吟。

translations.literal: With Longguang mutually responding in song, there was also Hundred Sorrows Chant.
translations.idiomatic: Among the poems he exchanged with Wang Longguang was Hundred Sorrows Chant.

sentences.zh: 龍光，字幼譽，浙江會稽人。

translations.literal: Longguang, style name Youyu, a man of Kuaiji in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Longguang, courtesy name Youyu, was from Kuaiji in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 諸生，屢躓鄉闈。

translations.literal: A licentiate, he repeatedly stumbled at the provincial examinations.
translations.idiomatic: A licensed scholar, he failed the provincial examinations again and again.

sentences.zh: 年五十餘，已倦遊，承謨撫浙，延課其子。

translations.literal: When over fifty years old, already weary of travel, Chengmo governed Zhejiang and extended an invitation to tutor his son.
translations.idiomatic: Past fifty and weary of wandering, he was invited by Fan Chengmo, then governor of Zhejiang, to tutor his son.

sentences.zh: 擢閩督，龍光以父老不欲行，父以承謨有德於浙，義不可辭，遂往。

translations.literal: Promoted to Fujian governor-general; Longguang because his father was old did not wish to go; his father said Chengmo had virtue toward Zhejiang and righteousness could not be declined, so he then went.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan was promoted to Fujian governor-general, Longguang hesitated because his father was elderly. His father insisted that Fan had done great good in Zhejiang and that duty forbade refusal, so he went.

sentences.zh: 既被執，脅草安民檄，誘以官爵，皆不從。

translations.literal: Once seized, he was compelled to draft a pacifying-the-people proclamation and enticed with official ranks; he did not comply in any case.
translations.idiomatic: After his arrest they forced him to write a proclamation to calm the people and tempted him with office and rank, but he would not yield on any point.

sentences.zh: 與永仁誼最合，嘗語龍光曰：「死之日，魂魄原無相離！」

translations.literal: His friendship with Yongren was closest; he once said to Longguang: "On the day of death, soul and spirit originally have no separation!"
translations.idiomatic: He was closest to Yongren and once told Longguang: when the day of death comes, our souls will not be parted!"

sentences.zh: 在獄著養花說及雜詩五十餘首以見志。

translations.literal: In prison he wrote On Cultivating Flowers and more than fifty miscellaneous poems to show his will.
translations.idiomatic: In prison he wrote On Cultivating Flowers and more than fifty lyric poems to declare his resolve.

sentences.zh: 天成，字上章，江南華亭人。

translations.literal: Tiancheng, style name Shangzhang, a man of Huating in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tiancheng, courtesy name Shangzhang, was from Huating in the lower Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 變作時，與永仁約同死。

translations.literal: When the uprising occurred, he agreed with Yongren to die together.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion broke out, he and Yongren pledged to die together.

sentences.zh: 偶外出，俄傳同難諸子死訊，遂出踐宿諾，為逆黨縛獻。

translations.literal: By chance he went out; soon came word that the fellows in calamity had all died; he then went out to fulfill his old pledge and was bound by the rebel faction and presented.
translations.idiomatic: He happened to be away, but when news came that his companions had been killed, he went out to keep his vow and was seized and handed over by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 時鞫者方窮究章奏，將歸罪永仁，天成厲聲辯曰：「承謨心事，青天白日，承謨無他志，書生更何與焉？」

translations.literal: At that time the interrogator was investigating memorials to the end and was about to assign guilt to Yongren; Tiancheng in a stern voice argued: "Chengmo's mind-set is blue sky and white sun; Chengmo had no other intent—what has a bookish man to do with it?"
translations.idiomatic: The interrogators were poring over official papers and were about to blame Yongren. Tiancheng cried out that Fan Chengmo's heart was as clear as the noonday sky, that he harbored no other design, and that a mere scholar had nothing to do with it."

sentences.zh: 乃同繫獄。

translations.literal: Then together they were imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was imprisoned along with the others.

sentences.zh: 著詩一卷，曰聽鵑。

translations.literal: He wrote one juan of poetry titled Listening to the Cuckoo.
translations.idiomatic: He left one scroll of verse, Listening to the Cuckoo.

sentences.zh: 又纂花譜一卷以自遣。

translations.literal: He also compiled one juan of a Flower Register to console himself.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled a Flower Register to pass the time.

sentences.zh: 三人在獄，有書名和淚譜者，龍光為永仁撰一首，永仁為龍光、天成撰各一首，詩詞皆燒桴煤畫牆上，賴義士林可棟者，或云泰宁人許鼎，時往獄中探視，默識之，得以傳世。

translations.literal: The three in prison had a book titled Tears-in-Harmony Collection; Longguang composed one piece for Yongren, Yongren composed one each for Longguang and Tiancheng; the poems were all drawn on the walls with burnt torch-pith; relying on the righteous scholar Lin Kedong, or some say Taining man Xu Ding, who at times went to the prison to visit and silently memorized them, they were thereby transmitted to the world.
translations.idiomatic: While the three were in prison they produced a collection called Tears-in-Harmony: Longguang wrote one poem for Yongren, and Yongren one each for Longguang and Tiancheng. They inscribed their verses on the walls with torch soot. The righteous scholar Lin Kedong—or, by another account, Xu Ding of Taining—visited the prison, memorized the poems in silence, and so preserved them for posterity.

sentences.zh: 承謨初被難，部曲有張福建者，手雙刀，大呼奪門，衛承謨，群攢刃死之。

translations.literal: When Chengmo first met calamity, among his retainers was one Zhang Fujian, who with paired sabers in hand loudly shouted to seize the gate and guard Chengmo; the band converged blades and he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Chengmo was first seized, a retainer named Zhang Fujian seized twin sabers, shouted to storm the gate, and tried to shield him. The mob closed in and cut him down.

sentences.zh: 精忠令三十二人監守承謨，中有蒙古人嘛尼，欲免承謨，事泄，被磔。

translations.literal: Jingzhong ordered thirty-two men to guard Chengmo; among them was a Mongol named Mani who wished to spare Chengmo; the affair leaked, and he was dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong set thirty-two men to guard Fan. Among them was a Mongol named Mani who tried to save him. When the plot was exposed, Mani was torn apart.

sentences.zh: 葉有挺，字貞夫，福建壽寧人。

translations.literal: Ye Youting, style name Zhenfu, a man of Shouning in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Youting, courtesy name Zhenfu, was from Shouning in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年進士，甫釋褐，即徒步南歸。

translations.literal: Advanced scholar in the ninth year of Kangxi; just upon shedding the brown robe he immediately went on foot south to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the ninth year of Kangxi and, as soon as he left office, walked home to the south.

sentences.zh: 耿精忠以閩叛，檄郡邑，凡在籍搢紳悉坐名，勒限​​起送，有挺恥之，潛入江西界，佯言已死。

translations.literal: Geng Jingzhong rebelled with Fujian, issued summons to prefectures and counties, and all local gentry-scholars on the register were seated by name and compelled within a limit to rise and be sent; Youting was ashamed of this, secretly entered the Jiangxi border, and falsely said he was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled in Fujian, he summoned every registered gentry-scholar by name and set a deadline for their delivery. Youting found this shameful, slipped into Jiangxi, and spread word that he had died.

sentences.zh: 逾年，以念母潛返，偽縣令偵知之，持檄促赴召。
