translations.literal: After more than a year, because he longed for his mother he secretly returned; the false magistrate detected and knew, held the summons, and urged him to answer the summons.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, longing for his mother, he stole home. The rebel magistrate learned of it and pressed him with a summons.

sentences.zh: 有挺告母曰：「兒得進士，思有以報君父。

translations.literal: Youting told his mother: "Your son obtained advanced-scholar status, thinking to have means to repay lord and father.
translations.idiomatic: Youting told his mother that he had become a metropolitan graduate hoping to repay his sovereign and father.

sentences.zh: 今以進士被偽檄，是得一進士反為從逆之資。

translations.literal: Now by advanced scholar receiving a false summons, this is obtaining one advanced scholar conversely becoming material for following the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Now that same degree is invoked by a rebel summons, turning my title into a credential for treason.

sentences.zh: 兒死不赴，如母何？」

translations.literal: Your son dies and will not go—what of mother?"
translations.idiomatic: I would rather die than obey, but what will become of you?"

sentences.zh: 母以大義勉之，乃抱母大號，遁匿山寺。

translations.literal: His mother with great righteousness urged him on; then embracing his mother he wailed loudly, fled, and hid in a mountain temple.
translations.idiomatic: His mother urged him on with the greater duty. He embraced her and wept, then fled to a mountain temple.

sentences.zh: 僧知其為葉進士也，微拒之，有挺仰天歎曰：「有挺豈以儒者七尺軀苟延旦夕，為釋氏恐怖？

translations.literal: The monk knew he was the Ye advanced scholar and slightly rejected him; Youting looked up to heaven and sighed: "Would Youting, with a Confucian scholar's seven-foot frame, prolong morning and evening out of fear of the Buddhist clergy?
translations.idiomatic: The monks recognized him as the Ye graduate and turned him away. Youting looked skyward and cried that he, a scholar seven feet tall, would not cling to life for fear of monks.

sentences.zh: 又豈以身死蕭寺，貽主僧禍？」

translations.literal: Again, would he die in a desolate temple and leave calamity for the chief monk?"
translations.idiomatic: And would I die in their temple and bring disaster on its abbot?"

sentences.zh: 夜起，北向九叩，南望母再叩，出走山下，自經古木死。

translations.literal: At night he rose, bowed nine times to the north, twice bowed southward toward his mother, went out below the mountain, and hanged himself on an ancient tree and died.
translations.idiomatic: That night he rose, kowtowed nine times to the north, twice toward his mother in the south, left the mountain, and hanged himself from an ancient tree.

sentences.zh: 亂平，無以上聞者，故褒贈皆不及。

translations.literal: When the rebellion was pacified there was none able to report upward, therefore commendation and posthumous gifts all did not reach him.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion ended no one reported his death, so he received no posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 同時閩中殉難者：蕭震，侯官人。

translations.literal: At the same time in Fujian those who died for righteousness included Xiao Zhen, a man of Houguan.
translations.idiomatic: Others in Fujian who died for the cause at the same time included Xiao Zhen of Houguan.

sentences.zh: 順治九年進士，任山西道監察御史，丁父艱，回籍。

translations.literal: Advanced scholar in the ninth year of Shunzhi; he served as investigating censor of the Shanxi Circuit, on father's mourning returned to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: A metropolitan graduate of the ninth year of Shunzhi, he served as investigating censor on the Shanxi circuit and returned home in mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 精忠叛，謀討之，事泄，遇害。

translations.literal: Jingzhong rebelled; he plotted to attack him; the affair leaked and he met with harm and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzhong rebelled he plotted resistance, but the plan was exposed and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 張松齡，莆田人。

translations.literal: Zhang Songling, a man of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Songling was a native of Putian.

sentences.zh: 順治十二年進士，由庶吉士屢遷四川參議。

translations.literal: Advanced scholar in the twelfth year of Shunzhi; from Hanlin bachelor he was repeatedly promoted to Sichuan vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: A graduate of the twelfth year of Shunzhi, he rose from Hanlin bachelor to vice commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 時川省彫敝，松齡加意撫綏，流亡漸復。

translations.literal: At that time Sichuan province was carved and exhausted; Songling added care to soothe and settle, and fugitives gradually returned.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan was then devastated, but Songling devoted himself to relief, and refugees gradually came home.

sentences.zh: 裁缺歸里，耿逆迫以偽職，羈數月，終不屈死。

translations.literal: His post was abolished and he returned home; the Geng rebel compelled him with a false office, detained him several months, and in the end he would not yield and died.
translations.idiomatic: When his post was abolished he went home. Geng's rebels pressed a false appointment on him, held him for months, and killed him when he refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 施大晁，福清人。

translations.literal: Shi Dachao, a man of Fuqing.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dachao was from Fuqing.

sentences.zh: 康熙十二年進士。

translations.literal: Advanced scholar in the twelfth year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the twelfth year of Kangxi.

sentences.zh: 聞變，匿金芝山，募壯士，助大兵進討，賊執之，嚼舌罵賊，嘔血數升死。

translations.literal: On hearing the uprising he hid on Golden Brocade Mountain, recruited stalwarts, and aided the great army in advancing to suppress; the rebels seized him, he chewed his tongue and cursed the rebels, vomited blood several sheng, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion broke out he hid on Golden Brocade Mountain, raised stalwarts, and aided the imperial advance. The rebels seized him; he bit through his tongue cursing them and died vomiting blood by the quart.

sentences.zh: 莆田舉人劉渭龍、建寧舉人謝邦協、南平舉人原任丹徒令鄒儀周，皆不受偽職。

translations.literal: Putian licentiate Liu Weilong, Jianning licentiate Xie Bangxie, and Nanping licentiate and former Dantu magistrate Zou Yizhou all did not accept false offices.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Weilong of Putian, Xie Bangxie of Jianning, and Zou Yizhou of Nanping—a licentiate and former magistrate of Dantu—all refused rebel appointments.

sentences.zh: 渭龍匿深山絕粒死。

translations.literal: Weilong hid in deep mountains, ceased grain, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Weilong hid deep in the mountains and starved himself to death.

sentences.zh: 邦協舉家避村落中，逆黨以火攻之，不出，闔門遇害。

translations.literal: Bangxie with his whole family avoided in a village; the rebel faction used fire to attack them; they did not come out, and the whole household met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Bangxie took his family to a village refuge. The rebels set fire to the house; they would not emerge, and the whole household perished.

sentences.zh: 儀周為所執，不屈死。

translations.literal: Yizhou was seized by them, would not yield, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou was captured and killed rather than submit.

sentences.zh: 光澤縣民毛錦生，素有力，賊躪其村，邑當事飭為練總，導大兵進剿，遇伏，死雲際關。

translations.literal: Guangze county commoner Mao Jinsheng, by nature possessed strength; rebels trampled his village; the county authorities ordered him as militia chief to guide the great army in advance suppression; he met an ambush and died at Yunji Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Jinsheng, a strong commoner of Guangze, saw rebels overrun his village. The county appointed him militia chief to guide imperial troops. He was ambushed and killed at Yunji Pass.

sentences.zh: 清流縣諸生李亭，隨邑令守城，並集鄉勇拒戰，旋被執，詈賊死。

translations.literal: Qingliu county licentiate Li Ting followed the county magistrate in defending the city, also gathered village braves to resist in battle, was soon seized, cursed the rebels, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ting, a licensed scholar of Qingliu, helped the magistrate defend the city and rallied village militia. He was soon captured, cursed the rebels, and died.

sentences.zh: 又有張存者，順昌人。

translations.literal: Also there was Zhang Cun, a man of Shunchang.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Zhang Cun of Shunchang.

sentences.zh: 精忠亂作，存糾義旅保元坑鄉，脅授總兵劄，令率眾出江西，分大軍兵勢，存不從。

translations.literal: When Jingzhong's rebellion arose, Cun gathered righteous militia to protect Yuan-keng township; they coerced him with appointment as grand marshal and ordered him to lead the masses out to Jiangxi to divide the great army's troop strength; Cun did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzhong rebelled, Cun raised a loyal militia to defend Yuan-keng. The rebels tried to appoint him grand marshal and send his men into Jiangxi to split the imperial forces, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 時和碩安親王岳樂駐師南昌，存潛使赴軍前乞援，併條上攻賊機宜。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of An, Noble Prince Yuelè, stationed troops at Nanchang; Cun secretly sent someone to the army front to beg aid and together listed plans for attacking the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuelè of the House of An held Nanchang. Cun secretly sent envoys to beg aid and laid out a plan of attack.

sentences.zh: 岳樂授存總兵劄，令捍禦建昌、邵武、汀州等地，且為內應。

translations.literal: Yuelè granted Cun a grand marshal patent and ordered him to defend Jianchang, Shaowu, Tingzhou, and other places, and also to act as an inside collaborator.
translations.idiomatic: Yuelè gave him a grand marshal's commission to hold Jianchang, Shaowu, Tingzhou, and the surrounding country as an imperial ally within rebel lines.

sentences.zh: 賊偵知之，急攻元坑。

translations.literal: The rebels detected and knew; they urgently attacked Yuan-keng.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels learned of it and stormed Yuan-keng.

sentences.zh: 地平，無險可扼，存以忠義激眾，屢敗賊，賊恚甚，分三路夾攻，卒以不支，存被執，死之。

translations.literal: The ground was level and there was no pass to hold; Cun with loyalty and righteousness inspired the masses and repeatedly defeated the rebels; the rebels were furious, divided three routes in a pincer attack, finally could not sustain, Cun was seized and died.
translations.idiomatic: The land was flat and offered no strongpoint, yet Cun roused his men with appeals to loyalty and beat the rebels again and again. Enraged, they attacked on three sides. Overwhelmed at last, he was captured and killed.

sentences.zh: 戴璣，字利衡，福建長泰人。

translations.literal: Dai Ji, style name Liheng, a man of Changtai in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Ji, courtesy name Liheng, was from Changtai in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 順治六年進士，授主事，例轉湖廣按察司僉事。

translations.literal: Advanced scholar in the sixth year of Shunzhi; appointed principal secretary, and by regulation transferred to vice commissioner of the Huguang surveillance commission.
translations.idiomatic: A metropolitan graduate of the sixth year of Shunzhi, he was appointed a principal secretary and then, by regulation, vice commissioner on the Huguang surveillance circuit.

sentences.zh: 時滇、黔未入版圖，上江防道尤要。

translations.literal: At that time Yunnan and Guizhou had not yet entered the territorial map, and the upper-river defense circuit was especially important.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan and Guizhou were not yet fully under Qing control, so the upper Yangtze defense circuit was especially critical.

sentences.zh: 璣遍履所部，自岳州至嘉魚，立七汛，造哨船巡邏，萑苻無警。

translations.literal: Ji everywhere trod his jurisdiction; from Yuezhou to Jiayu he established seven river stations, built sentry boats to patrol, and brushwood bandits had no alarm.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled his entire circuit, from Yuezhou to Jiayu, establishing seven river posts and patrol boats until bandits along the banks gave no trouble.

sentences.zh: 又於洞庭湖接立三汛，行者尤便之。

translations.literal: He also connected and established three stations on Dongting Lake; travelers especially found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He added three linked posts on Dongting Lake, which travelers found especially convenient.

sentences.zh: 洪承疇正經略五省，以「韓、範儔」稱之。

translations.literal: Hong Chengchou was then rectifying the five provinces and called him "a match for Han and Fan."
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chengchou, then directing five provinces, compared him to Han Xin and Fan Li.

sentences.zh: 尋遷陝西西寧道，未行，丁父艱。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Shaanxi Xining circuit but had not yet departed when he entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to the Xining circuit in Shaanxi but had not taken up the post when his father died.

sentences.zh: 服除，補廣西右江道，駐柳州。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was supplemented to the Guangxi Right River circuit and stationed at Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was appointed to the Right River circuit in Guangxi and stationed at Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 東闌土酋構禍日久，璣以恩意調解之。

translations.literal: The native chiefs of the eastern pass had long framed disasters; Ji mediated them with gracious intent.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal chiefs of the eastern frontier had long been at odds; he settled disputes through conciliation.

sentences.zh: 大酋黃應元煽亂，則斬渠魁以徇。

translations.literal: When the great chief Huang Yingyuan stirred rebellion, he beheaded the ringleaders to display.
translations.idiomatic: When the great chief Huang Yingyuan incited revolt, he executed the ringleaders as an example.

sentences.zh: 諸蠻用是懷德畏威，頑梗盡化。

translations.literal: The various Man thereby cherished virtue and feared authority, and obstinate defiance all transformed.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes thereafter honored his kindness and feared his power, and stubborn resistance melted away.

sentences.zh: 柳堡屯田，寄佃於民，既輸軍租，复應民役，為申請督撫，具奏獲免。

translations.literal: Liubao garrison fields were contracted to common people as tenancy; having paid military rent they again answered commoners' corvée; he memorialized to the governor and governor-general, submitted a memorial, and obtained exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Tenants on the Liubao garrison fields paid military rent yet were still liable for local labor service. He petitioned the governor and governor-general and won them exemption.

sentences.zh: 復修葺文廟及羅池司戶二賢祠。

translations.literal: He again repaired and refurbished the Confucian temple and the Two Worthies Shrine of the Luo Pool registrar.
translations.idiomatic: He also restored the Confucian temple and the shrine to the Two Worthies of the Luo Pool registrar.

sentences.zh: 會朝命裁併監司，解任歸里，督課諸子，教以忠孝大義。

translations.literal: At court order to merge and reduce surveillance commissioners, he was relieved of office and returned home, supervised his sons' studies, and taught them loyalty and filial piety's great meaning.
translations.idiomatic: When the court ordered a reduction of surveillance posts, he retired home, tutored his sons, and taught them the great duties of loyalty and filial piety.

sentences.zh: 耿精忠亂作，台灣賊圍漳州，時璣次子鏻為海澄公將，守東門。

translations.literal: When Geng Jingzhong's rebellion arose, Taiwan rebels besieged Zhangzhou; at that time Ji's second son Lin was a general of the Duke of Haicheng and guarded the east gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled, Taiwan forces besieged Zhangzhou. Dai's second son Lin, a general under the Duke of Haicheng, held the east gate.

sentences.zh: 賊劫至城下，使招鏻降。

translations.literal: Rebels raided to below the walls and sent envoys to summon Lin to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pressed to the walls and sent envoys urging Lin to surrender.

sentences.zh: 璣大聲呼鏻堅守，勿以老人為念。

translations.literal: Ji loudly called to Lin to hold firm and not take the old man into mind.
translations.idiomatic: Dai shouted to Lin to stand fast and pay no heed to an old man's fate.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，牽去。

translations.literal: The rebels were angry and dragged him away.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the rebels dragged him off.

sentences.zh: 城破，鏻巷戰死，闔門為俘。

translations.literal: The city was broken; Lin died fighting in the lanes, and the whole household became captives.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell. Lin died fighting in the streets, and the whole household was taken captive.

sentences.zh: 大兵复漳州，賊遁，璣與子鈃等乘間入山，而妻葉併諸幼子為賊執赴台灣，璣置不為意。

translations.literal: The great army recaptured Zhangzhou and the rebels fled; Ji with his son Ming and others seized an interval to enter the mountains, while his wife Ye together with the young sons was seized by rebels and taken to Taiwan; Ji set his mind on it without concern.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial troops retook Zhangzhou and the rebels fled. Dai slipped into the hills with his son Ming and others, while his wife Ye and younger sons were carried off to Taiwan—a loss he refused to brood over.

sentences.zh: 賊复犯海澄及長泰，璣再被執，脅之降，不從。

translations.literal: The rebels again attacked Haicheng and Changtai; Ji was again seized and compelled to surrender, but he did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels struck Haicheng and Changtai again, he was captured once more and pressed to submit, but he would not.

sentences.zh: 幽之密室，歷年餘，終不為屈，朝夕誦文信公正氣歌以自壯。

translations.literal: They confined him in a secret chamber for more than a year; in the end he would not bend, morning and evening reciting Lord Wen's Song of Righteous Spirit to bolster himself.
translations.idiomatic: They shut him in a hidden room for more than a year, yet he never broke. Morning and night he recited Wen Tianxiang's Song of Righteous Spirit to steel himself.

sentences.zh: 一日，顧謂子銑曰：「吾久辱，不死何為？」

translations.literal: One day, turning to his son Xin he said: "I have long been disgraced—not dying for what?"
translations.idiomatic: One day he turned to his son Xin and said he had borne this shame long enough and asked why he should linger in life."

sentences.zh: 遂絕粒。

translations.literal: Then he ceased grain.
translations.idiomatic: He stopped eating.

sentences.zh: 數日，病甚，衣冠，命銑扶掖北向再拜，曰：「臣死，命也，當為厲鬼殺賊！」

translations.literal: After several days his illness was severe; dressed in cap and gown, he ordered Xin to support him northward to bow twice and said: "Your subject dies—fate it is; I ought to become a vengeful ghost and kill rebels!"
translations.idiomatic: Days later, gravely ill, he donned cap and gown, had Xin help him bow twice to the north, and declared that a subject's death was fate's decree and that he would become a vengeful ghost to slay rebels.

sentences.zh: 索紙筆，大書「惟忠惟孝，可以服人」數字，嘔血數升死，年七十有四。

translations.literal: He sought paper and brush, in large characters wrote the words "Only loyalty, only filial piety can subdue people," vomited blood several sheng, and died at age seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He called for brush and ink and wrote in bold characters: only loyalty and filial piety can win men's hearts. He vomited blood by the quart and died at seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 劉欽鄰，江南儀徵人。

translations.literal: Liu Qinlin, Jiangnan Yizheng person.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qinlin was a native of Yizheng in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 順治十八年進士。

translations.literal: Shunzhi eighteenth year jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighteenth year of Shunzhi.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，授廣西富川縣知縣。

translations.literal: Kangxi eighth year, bestowed Guangxi Fuchuan County magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Kangxi he was appointed magistrate of Fuchuan County in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 十三年，廣西將軍孫延齡叛應吳三桂，遣偽將陷平樂府，旋圍富川。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year, Guangxi General Sun Yanling rebelled responding to Wu Sangui, dispatched false general to seize Pingle Prefecture, shortly besieged Fuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, Guangxi General Sun Yanling rebelled in support of Wu Sangui, sent a rebel general to take Pingle Prefecture, and soon encircled Fuchuan.

sentences.zh: 欽鄰募鄉勇城守，與賊相拒五十餘日。

translations.literal: Qinlin recruited village braves to defend the city, with rebels mutually resisted fifty-odd days.
translations.idiomatic: Qinlin raised local militia to hold the walls and kept the rebels at bay for more than fifty days.

sentences.zh: 同城把總楊虎受延齡偽劄，勾土賊千餘助攻，虎夜引賊入，欽鄰率家丁力戰，殺賊三十餘，家丁死者七，欽鄰被執。

translations.literal: Same-city Corporal of the Guard Yang Hu received Yanling's false dispatch, colluded with native bandits over a thousand to assist the attack; Hu at night led rebels in; Qinlin led household retainers to fight fiercely, killed rebels thirty-odd, household retainers dead seven, Qinlin was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu, a garrison corporal in the same city, accepted a forged order from Yanling and rallied more than a thousand native bandits to join the assault; at night Hu let the rebels inside. Qinlin led his household retainers in a desperate fight, killing more than thirty rebels; seven retainers fell and Qinlin was captured.

sentences.zh: 賊加以毒刑，縛送桂林。

translations.literal: Rebels applied cruel torture, bound and sent to Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels tortured him savagely and sent him bound to Guilin.

sentences.zh: 延齡誘降，不屈，羈之。

translations.literal: Yanling induced surrender; he did not submit, detained him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling tried to win him over; he refused to yield and was held prisoner.

sentences.zh: 欽鄰賦絕命詞死，追諡忠節。

translations.literal: Qinlin composed a death poem and died; posthumously enfeoffed with the title Loyal Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Qinlin wrote a farewell poem and died; he was posthumously honored with the title Zhongjie (Loyal Integrity).

sentences.zh: 崔成嵐，鑲藍旗漢軍。

translations.literal: Cui Chenglan, Bordered Blue Banner Han Army.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Chenglan was a Han bannerman of the Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 由官學生任鬱林州州判，署藤縣知縣。

translations.literal: From Imperial Academy student served as Yulin Prefecture assistant prefect, acting Teng County magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as an Imperial Academy student, he served as assistant prefect of Yulin Prefecture and acted as magistrate of Teng County.

sentences.zh: 十四年，孫延齡黨吳鳳等率賊數千犯藤縣，水陸夾攻，成嵐與守備劉志高、汪雲龍，典史黃新德守禦。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year, Sun Yanling's partisan Wu Feng and others led rebels several thousand to attack Teng County, water and land pincer attack; Chenglan with Garrison Commander Liu Zhigao, Wang Yunlong, and Registrar Huang Xinde defended.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, Wu Feng and other partisans of Sun Yanling led several thousand rebels against Teng County in a combined land-and-water assault; Chenglan, Garrison Commanders Liu Zhigao and Wang Yunlong, and Registrar Huang Xinde mounted the defense.

sentences.zh: 賊暫退，巳而復合。

translations.literal: Rebels briefly withdrew, presently gathered again.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels withdrew for a time, then regrouped and returned.

sentences.zh: 延齡軍數千，攻城西南，抵禦益力。

translations.literal: Yanling's army several thousand attacked the city from the southwest; resistance grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand of Yanling's troops assaulted the southwest wall, and the defenders fought back all the harder.

sentences.zh: 巡撫洪陳明復遣援兵，協力剿殺，賊不退。

translations.literal: Governor Hong Chenming again dispatched relief troops; together they strove to exterminate and kill, yet rebels did not withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Hong Chenming sent reinforcements again, and all sides fought to destroy the enemy, but the rebels would not pull back.

sentences.zh: 偽將軍緱成德复率賊萬餘由賀縣來，勢益熾。

translations.literal: False General Gou Chengde again led rebels over ten thousand from He County; momentum grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Gou Chengde then marched from He County with more than ten thousand men, and the rebel strength surged.

sentences.zh: 成嵐等相持七晝夜，城陷，成嵐手刃二賊，歿於陣，志高等均死之。

translations.literal: Chenglan and others held out seven days and nights; the city fell; Chenglan with his own hand slew two rebels and perished in battle; Zhigao and the rest all died.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglan and his comrades held out for seven days and nights until the city fell; Chenglan killed two rebels with his own blade and died in the fighting, and Zhigao and the others all perished as well.

sentences.zh: 新德，廣東海陽人。

translations.literal: Xinde, Guangdong Haiyang person.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Xinde was a native of Haiyang in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 讀書不多，好遣文，人皆笑之。

translations.literal: His reading was not extensive; he loved to compose literary pieces, and everyone laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: He had little schooling but loved to write polished prose, which made him a figure of ridicule.

sentences.zh: 事亟時，命其子日禱扶母歸養。

translations.literal: When affairs were urgent, he ordered his son Ritao to support his mother and return home to care for her.
translations.idiomatic: As the crisis deepened, he told his son Ritao to escort his mother home for her upkeep.

sentences.zh: 既被執，賊欲授以偽官，新德曰：「王彥章且不肯降唐，況天朝臣子從賊乎？」

translations.literal: Once seized, rebels wished to grant him a false office; Xinde said: "Wang Yanzhang would not even submit to Tang—how much less should a subject of the Celestial Dynasty follow rebels?"
translations.idiomatic: After he was taken, the rebels offered him a post in their regime; Xinde replied that even Wang Yanzhang had refused to bow to the Tang, so how could a servant of the dynasty join rebels?"

sentences.zh: 賊欲屠城，新德曰：「倡守城者，官也，殺尉足矣，於百姓何與？」

translations.literal: Rebels wished to massacre the city; Xinde said: "Those who urged defense of the city were the officials—killing the assistant magistrate is enough; what has that to do with the common people?"
translations.idiomatic: When they threatened to slaughter the town, he said the officials alone had urged resistance and that killing the registrar would suffice—the common people had no part in it."

sentences.zh: 賊怒，斮之，新德罵不絕口。

translations.literal: Rebels were enraged and hacked him; Xinde cursed without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels in fury hacked him to pieces while Xinde never stopped cursing them.

sentences.zh: 刀斧交下，碎其屍。

translations.literal: Blades and axes fell together, shattering his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Blades and axes rained down until his body was torn apart.

sentences.zh: 家人四，婢一，皆死焉。

translations.literal: Family members four, maidservant one—all died.
translations.idiomatic: Four members of his household and one maidservant died with him.

sentences.zh: 微官死事，世尤重之。

translations.literal: A petty official dying for his duty—the age especially esteems this.
translations.idiomatic: That a minor official should die for his post won him exceptional esteem.

sentences.zh: 柯永昇，漢軍鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: Ke Yongsheng, Han Army Bordered Red Banner person.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Yongsheng was a Han bannerman of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 由員外郎出任湖南糧道，累擢至湖廣巡撫。

translations.literal: From Departmental Director he went out to serve as Hunan Grain Intendant, and by successive promotions reached Huguang Governor.
translations.idiomatic: He left the post of Departmental Director to become Hunan Grain Intendant and rose step by step to governor of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十七年，飭裁湖廣總督，令標兵分別存撤。

translations.literal: Kangxi twenty-seventh year, he was ordered to trim the Huguang Governor-General's establishment and directed the banner garrison troops to be kept or dismissed as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Kangxi he was charged with reducing the Huguang governor-general's forces and with deciding which garrison troops to retain or disband.

sentences.zh: 五月，裁兵夏逢龍，同夥呼為夏包子者，結眾作亂。

translations.literal: Fifth month, dismissed soldier Xia Fenglong—his companions called him Steamed-bun Xia—gathered a crowd and made rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the demobilized soldier Xia Fenglong, nicknamed Steamed-bun Xia by his fellows, rallied a mob and rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 二十二日，突入巡撫署，拒者輒刃之。

translations.literal: On the twenty-second day they burst into the governor's yamen; whoever resisted was at once bladed.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-second they stormed the governor's compound and cut down anyone who stood in their way.

sentences.zh: 傷永昇臂，奪其印，复傷永昇足，僕地。

translations.literal: They wounded Yongsheng's arm, seized his seal, again wounded Yongsheng's foot, and he fell prostrate.
translations.idiomatic: They wounded Yongsheng's arm and seized his seal, then struck his leg and knocked him to the ground.

sentences.zh: 悉驅其親屬家人出走，搜掠財物。

translations.literal: They drove out all his kin and household, and plundered goods.
translations.idiomatic: They drove out his family and retainers and looted his property.

sentences.zh: 永昇乘間自縊死。

translations.literal: Yongsheng seized an interval and hanged himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yongsheng seized a moment alone and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 賊四出剽略，永州錦田衛守備隨光啟嬰城守，力竭，死之。

translations.literal: Rebels ranged in all directions to plunder; Yongzhou Jintian Guard Garrison Commander Sui Guangqi defended the city with walls, strength exhausted, and died.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fanned out to pillage; Sui Guangqi, garrison commander at Jintian Guard in Yongzhou, held the walls until his strength gave out and he died.

sentences.zh: 武昌永定營中軍守備孟泰鏖戰金口，亦中砲歿。

translations.literal: Wuchang Yongding Battalion Central Army Garrison Commander Meng Tai fought fiercely at Jinkou and likewise was struck by cannon and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Tai, central-army garrison commander of the Yongding Battalion at Wuchang, fought bitterly at Jinkou and was killed by cannon fire.

sentences.zh: 守備李國俊陽附逢龍，從圍應城。

translations.literal: Garrison Commander Li Guojun outwardly joined Fenglong and followed in besieging Yingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison Commander Li Guojun pretended to side with Fenglong and marched with him to besiege Yingcheng.

sentences.zh: 夜半，賊潛梯登城，國俊遽鳴鉦大呼，城中驚起，擊敗之。

translations.literal: At midnight rebels secretly scaled the wall on ladders; Guojun hastily sounded the gong and shouted; the city startled awake and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight the rebels tried to scale the walls on ladders; Guojun suddenly rang the gong and shouted the alarm, the city roused itself, and the assault was beaten off.

sentences.zh: 脫還武昌，卒死樊口。

translations.literal: He escaped back to Wuchang and ultimately died at Fankou.
translations.idiomatic: He made his way back to Wuchang but eventually died at Fankou.

sentences.zh: 時署布政使者為葉映榴，自有傳。

translations.literal: At the time the acting Provincial Administration Commissioner was Ye Yingliu; he has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: The acting provincial treasurer at the time was Ye Yingliu, who has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 道禪，滿洲鑲黃旗人，姓戴佳。

translations.literal: Dao Chan, Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner person, surname Daijia.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Chan was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner, clan name Daijia.

sentences.zh: 初為王府長史。

translations.literal: At first he was a princely establishment Chief Steward.
translations.idiomatic: He began as chief steward of a princely establishment.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，厄魯特噶勒丹犯喀爾喀，朝命中外備兵。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi reign, the Oirat Galdan invaded Khalkha; the court ordered inner and outer preparations of troops.
translations.idiomatic: During Kangxi's reign the Oirat leader Galdan invaded Khalkha Mongolia, and the court ordered forces readied throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，大兵三路進剿，道禪奉敕往諭噶勒丹。

translations.literal: Thirty-fifth year, the great army advanced in three routes to suppress; Dao Chan received the edict to go admonish Galdan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year the main forces advanced on three fronts; Dao Chan was ordered to go and deliver the imperial message to Galdan.

sentences.zh: 先是，三十一年，員外郎瑪第奉使策妄阿喇布坦，為噶勒丹掠執，不屈死。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the thirty-first year, Departmental Director Ma Di was sent on mission to Tsewang Arabtan, was seized by Galdan, would not submit, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the thirty-first year, Departmental Director Ma Di had been sent to Tsewang Arabtan, was captured by Galdan, refused to yield, and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 至是賊复誘降，道禪抗聲罵賊，死之。

translations.literal: At this the rebels again induced surrender; Dao Chan raised his voice and cursed the rebels, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Now the enemy again tried to win him over; Dao Chan shouted curses at them and was killed.

sentences.zh: 李茂吉，福建漳浦人。

translations.literal: Li Maoji, Fujian Zhangpu person.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maoji was a native of Zhangpu in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 台灣水師營把總，平日不以官小自卑。

translations.literal: Taiwan Naval Battalion Corporal of the Guard; on ordinary days he did not because of petty rank belittle himself.
translations.idiomatic: He was a corporal in the Taiwan naval battalion and never let his low rank diminish his sense of duty.

sentences.zh: 康熙六十年，土賊朱一貴亂作，自請於副將許雲。

translations.literal: Kangxi sixtieth year, native bandit Zhu Yigui's rebellion arose; he volunteered himself to Vice General Xu Yun.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year of Kangxi, when the rebel Zhu Yigui rose, he volunteered for service under Vice General Xu Yun.

sentences.zh: 戰敗被擒，賊渠怪其不跪，叱之，茂吉舉足踢其案，案翻，奮力斷縛，直前奪刀殺賊。

translations.literal: Defeated in battle and seized, the rebel chieftain wondered at his not kneeling and scolded him; Maoji raised his foot and kicked his desk; the desk overturned; he strove with force to break his bonds, went straight forward, seized a blade, and killed rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated and captured, the rebel chief rebuked him for refusing to kneel; Maoji kicked the man's desk over, broke his bonds, rushed forward, snatched a sword, and killed several rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊共斫之，頭腦破裂，尚罵不絕口，賊碎其屍。

translations.literal: Rebels together hacked him; his skull burst, yet he still cursed without cease; rebels shattered his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels hacked him down until his skull was split open, yet he never stopped cursing; they tore his body to pieces.

sentences.zh: 劉琨，字玉岩，四川保寧人。

translations.literal: Liu Kun, style Yuyan, Sichuan Baoning person.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun, styled Yuyan, was a native of Baoning in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 由武舉從軍有功。

translations.literal: From military licentiate he followed the army with merit.
translations.idiomatic: A military licentiate, he entered service and distinguished himself in the field.

sentences.zh: 雍正八年，擢權雲南東烏營游擊，佐總兵劉起元守城。

translations.literal: Yongzheng eighth year, promoted to acting Yunnan Dongwu Battalion Mobile Brigade Commander, assisting Regional Commander Liu Qiyuan in defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yongzheng he was made acting mobile brigade commander of the Dongwu Battalion in Yunnan and helped Regional Commander Liu Qiyuan hold the city.

sentences.zh: 烏蒙夷祿萬福者，舊土知府萬鍾族弟也。

translations.literal: The Wumeng Yi Lu Wanfu was the former native prefect Wan Zhong's younger clansman.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wanfu of the Wumeng Yi was a younger kinsman of the former native prefect Wan Zhong.

sentences.zh: 先是，府隸四川，萬鍾數擾雲南邊界，雲貴總督鄂爾泰擒鞫伏法，使萬福父鼎坤襲職，移隸雲南。

translations.literal: Earlier the prefecture was subordinate to Sichuan; Wan Zhong repeatedly disturbed Yunnan's borders; Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Ortai seized, tried, and executed him by law, had Wanfu's father Ding Kun inherit the post, and transferred subordination to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: The district had formerly been under Sichuan; Wan Zhong had repeatedly raided the Yunnan frontier until Governor-General Ortai captured him, tried him, and put him to death, installing Wanfu's father Ding Kun in his place and placing the territory under Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 時改土歸流，既設東川府，次及烏蒙，改授鼎坤守備，趣赴闕。

translations.literal: At the time of replacing native chiefs with appointed officials, after Dongchuan Prefecture was established, next came Wumeng; Ding Kun was changed to Garrison Commander and urged to proceed to court.
translations.idiomatic: As the court replaced native rule with regular administration, it had already set up Dongchuan Prefecture and next turned to Wumeng, reassigning Ding Kun as garrison commander and summoning him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 鼎坤怏怏行，密使萬福煽諸蠻為亂。

translations.literal: Ding Kun went resentfully; secretly he sent Wanfu to incite the various barbarians to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Kun set out in sullen resentment and secretly ordered Wanfu to stir the tribes into revolt.

sentences.zh: 未發，琨密告起元為備，起元蔑視之，檄萬福來見。

translations.literal: Before it broke out, Kun secretly informed Qiyuan to prepare; Qiyuan despised this, and dispatched a summons for Wanfu to come and appear.
translations.idiomatic: Before the plot erupted, Kun secretly warned Qiyuan to prepare; Qiyuan dismissed the warning and issued a summons for Wanfu to present himself.

sentences.zh: 萬福懼，遂嗾眾反，圍府城。

translations.literal: Wanfu feared this, then incited the masses to rebel and besieged the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: Wanfu, alarmed, incited his followers to rise and encircled the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 琨聞變，解所佩刀與妻張氏訣，出與起元商禦賊策，皆不應。

translations.literal: Kun heard of the uprising, unfastened the blade at his belt and took leave of his wife Lady Zhang, went out to discuss with Qiyuan strategies to repel rebels—all without response.
translations.idiomatic: When Kun heard of the revolt he gave his belt sword to his wife Lady Zhang in farewell, then went to Qiyuan to discuss how to fight the rebels, but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 而游擊汪仁獨以撫賊說起元，起元從之，登城被賊辱。

translations.literal: Yet Mobile Brigade Commander Wang Ren alone used pacifying rebels to persuade Qiyuan; Qiyuan followed this, ascended the wall, and was insulted by rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Only Mobile Brigade Commander Wang Ren urged Qiyuan to appease the enemy; Qiyuan listened, went up on the wall, and was humiliated by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 琨遂開城，率數十騎大呼赴賊，游擊馬秉倫與之俱。

translations.literal: Kun then opened the city gate, led several tens of horsemen shouting as they charged the rebels; Mobile Brigade Commander Ma Binglun went with him.
translations.idiomatic: Kun then threw open the gates, led several dozen horsemen in a shouting charge at the enemy, and Mobile Brigade Commander Ma Binglun rode with him.

sentences.zh: 斬數百級，賊稍卻。

translations.literal: They beheaded several hundred heads; rebels slightly withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They cut down hundreds of the enemy and the rebels fell back somewhat.

sentences.zh: 野夷數万蜂至，琨遂與秉倫相失，勢益孤。

translations.literal: Wild tribesmen in the tens of thousands swarmed like bees; Kun then lost contact with Binglun, and his position grew lonelier.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of tribal fighters swarmed in; Kun was separated from Binglun and his position grew desperate.

sentences.zh: 轉戰至次日，弩穿左脅，創甚，北向再拜，割襟蘸血，大書石壁曰「淋漓鮮血透征衣，報國丹心總不移」十四字，拔刀自刎死。

translations.literal: Fighting turned until the next day; a crossbow bolt pierced his left flank, wounds severe; he bowed twice to the north, cut his collar and dipped blood, in large script on the stone wall wrote the fourteen characters "Streaming fresh blood soaks the campaign robe; the loyal heart to serve the state never shifts," drew his blade and cut his own throat to die.
translations.idiomatic: He fought on into the next day until a bolt pierced his left side; gravely wounded, he bowed twice toward the north, cut his robe to write in his own blood on a cliff face fourteen characters—"Streaming fresh blood soaks the campaign robe; the loyal heart to serve the state never shifts"—then drew his sword and took his own life.

sentences.zh: 賊歎其忠，以土覆之而去。

translations.literal: Rebels sighed at his loyalty, covered him with earth, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels marveled at his loyalty, covered him with earth, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 琨妻聞變，則以琨佩刀手斫二女及妾，乃引刀椿喉，一門同殉焉，語見列女傳。

translations.literal: Kun's wife heard of the uprising, then with Kun's belt blade with her own hand hacked his two daughters and concubine, then drew the blade to her throat; the whole household together followed in martyrdom—the account appears in the Biographies of Exemplary Women.
translations.idiomatic: When Kun's wife heard what had happened, she took his sword and killed their two daughters and his concubine, then turned the blade on her own throat; the whole household perished with him, as told in the Biographies of Exemplary Women.

sentences.zh: 秉倫既失琨，亦轉山箐間，鏢貫其頤，猶手剸數賊，力竭，跳崖死。

translations.literal: Binglun having lost Kun, also turned among mountain ravines; a dart pierced his jaw, yet he still with his hand slaughtered several rebels; strength exhausted, he leapt from a cliff and died.
translations.idiomatic: Separated from Kun, Binglun fought on through the mountain passes; a dart pierced his jaw, yet he still killed several rebels by hand before, spent, he leapt from a cliff to his death.

sentences.zh: 時官烏蒙通判者為劉鎮寶。

translations.literal: At the time the Wumeng Subprefect was Liu Zhenbao.
translations.idiomatic: The subprefect of Wumeng at the time was Liu Zhenbao.

sentences.zh: 鎮寶，字楚善，江西彭澤人。

translations.literal: Zhenbao, style Chushan, Jiangxi Pengze person.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhenbao, styled Chushan, was a native of Pengze in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 由舉人考授中書舍人，發雲南用知縣。

translations.literal: From provincial graduate he passed examination for Secretariat Drafter, was dispatched to Yunnan and used as county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate, he qualified as a Secretariat drafter and was sent to Yunnan to serve as a county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 鄂爾泰器其材，奏擢通判。

translations.literal: Ortai valued his talent and memorialized to promote him to Subprefect.
translations.idiomatic: Ortai admired his ability and memorialized the throne to promote him to subprefect.

sentences.zh: 鎮寶既蒞任，駐大關鎮，鎮距府三百里，為苗疆新闢地。

translations.literal: Once Zhenbao had assumed office, he stationed at Daguan Town; the town was three hundred li from the prefectural seat and was newly opened Miao frontier land.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office Zhenbao was posted to Daguan Town, three hundred li from the prefectural seat in newly pacified Miao territory.

sentences.zh: 苗警既急，以鎮寶熟諳苗情，檄往招諭。

translations.literal: Miao alarms already urgent, because Zhenbao was well versed in Miao conditions, he was dispatched by edict to go summon and admonish.
translations.idiomatic: As the Miao unrest grew acute, he was ordered out to parley because he knew the tribes well.

sentences.zh: 至則開陳禍福，詞甚備。

translations.literal: On arrival he set forth fortune and misfortune; his words were very complete.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he laid out the rewards of peace and the cost of rebellion in full detail.

sentences.zh: 苗逆抗之，反執鎮寶。

translations.literal: Miao rebels resisted him and instead seized Zhenbao.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Miao resisted and seized him instead.

sentences.zh: 鎮寶罵賊烈，爭斫之，支體糜碎。

translations.literal: Zhenbao cursed the rebels fiercely; they vied to hack him; his limbs were pulverized.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenbao cursed them fiercely; they hacked at him in a frenzy until his body was torn to shreds.

sentences.zh: 事平，滇人以鎮寶與琨受害尤酷，為立廟祀，稱二劉公祠。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, Yunnan people because Zhenbao and Kun suffered especially cruelly, erected a temple to worship them, called the Two Lords Liu Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored, the people of Yunnan, who saw Zhenbao and Kun as having suffered especially cruel deaths, built a temple in their honor called the Shrine of the Two Lords Liu.

sentences.zh: 羅鳴序，湖北漢陽人。

translations.literal: Luo Mingxu, Hubei Hanyang person.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Mingxu was a native of Hanyang in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十年舉人，任貴州麻哈知州、兼署黃平州事。

translations.literal: Kangxi fiftieth year provincial graduate; served as Guizhou Maha Prefect and concurrently acted in Huangping Prefecture affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate of the fiftieth year of Kangxi, he was prefect of Maha in Guizhou and also acted as administrator of Huangping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 雍正十三年春，古州苗叛，脅清平、黃平、施秉、鎮遠四州縣，生熟苗皆應。

translations.literal: Yongzheng thirteenth year spring, Guzhou Miao rebelled, coerced Qingping, Huangping, Shibing, Zhenyuan four prefectures and counties; raw and cooked Miao all responded.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the thirteenth year of Yongzheng the Guzhou Miao rebelled, threatening Qingping, Huangping, Shibing, and Zhenyuan, and both settled and wild Miao joined them.

sentences.zh: 四月，陷清平縣之凱里汛，去黃平新州三十里。

translations.literal: Fourth month, seized Qingping County's Kaili garrison post, thirty li from Huangping's new prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month they took the Kaili garrison in Qingping County, thirty li from the new seat of Huangping.

sentences.zh: 鳴序時在黃平，聞變，趨新州謀守禦。

translations.literal: Mingxu was then at Huangping; hearing of the uprising, he hastened to the new prefectural seat to plan defense.
translations.idiomatic: Mingxu was at Huangping when he heard the news and rushed to the new prefectural seat to organize a defense.

sentences.zh: 環州苗皆起，馳報府縣急援，不應。

translations.literal: Miao all around the prefecture rose; he galloped to report to prefecture and county for urgent relief—no response.
translations.idiomatic: Miao throughout the district rose; he sent urgent pleas to the prefectural and county authorities for help, but none came.

sentences.zh: 苗大焚掠，鳴序以城亡與亡自誓。

translations.literal: Miao greatly burned and plundered; Mingxu with the city's fall and his own fall made a vow.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao burned and looted on a wide scale; Mingxu swore he would perish with the city.

sentences.zh: 客陳憲者，請與俱，鳴序卻之。

translations.literal: A guest, Chen Xian, asked to go with him; Mingxu declined him.
translations.idiomatic: His guest Chen Xian asked to stay with him, but Mingxu refused.

sentences.zh: 憲以「君能為忠臣，我獨不能為義士」為對，相與尋後山有樹可援系者，各默識之。

translations.literal: Xian replied, "You can be a loyal minister—can I alone not be a righteous man?" Together they sought on the rear hill trees by which one could grasp and tie; each silently marked them.
translations.idiomatic: Xian answered, "If you can die a loyal minister, why should I alone not die a righteous man?" Together they found trees on the hill behind the city suitable for hanging and each quietly noted the spot.

sentences.zh: 鳴序乃解兩州印付健僕送省，出公帑千付書吏藏某處，曰：「可以死矣！」

translations.literal: Mingxu then unfastened the two prefectures' seals and gave them to a sturdy servant to send to the province, took out a thousand taels of public funds for the clerk to hide in a certain place, and said: "One may die now!"
translations.idiomatic: Mingxu sent the seals of both prefectures to the provincial capital by a trusted servant, entrusted a thousand taels of public funds to a clerk to hide, and said, "Now I can die!"

sentences.zh: 或曰：「此署事也，有本州在，何不去此而保麻哈？」

translations.literal: Someone said: "This is acting duty; the home prefecture is there—why not leave here and preserve Maha?"
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him that this was only an acting post while his own prefecture of Maha was safe, so why not withdraw there?"

sentences.zh: 或曰：「此新州也，何不去此而保舊州？」

translations.literal: Someone said: "This is the new prefectural seat—why not leave here and preserve the old prefectural seat?"
translations.idiomatic: Others said this was only the new prefectural seat and asked why he did not fall back to the old one."

sentences.zh: 皆置不聽。

translations.literal: He set all aside and did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He ignored every suggestion.

sentences.zh: 或告曰：「城陷矣！」

translations.literal: Someone reported: "The city has fallen!"
translations.idiomatic: Someone cried that the city had fallen."

sentences.zh: 即趨向所識處，將自經。

translations.literal: He at once hastened toward the place he had marked and was about to hang himself.
translations.idiomatic: He hurried to the tree he had chosen and was about to hang himself.

sentences.zh: 俄又告賊猶未入，則又徐與憲還，登城守。

translations.literal: Shortly someone again reported the rebels had not yet entered; then he again slowly with Xian returned and ascended the wall to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later word came that the enemy had not yet broken in, so he and Xian walked back and took up the defense on the walls again.

sentences.zh: 迨矢石器械盡，城中火起，無可再守，乃卒與憲至後山絓樹以死。

translations.literal: When arrows, stones, and weapons were exhausted, fire arose within the city, and there was no way to defend further; then at last with Xian he went to the rear hill, looped ropes on trees, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When arrows, stones, and arms were spent and fire broke out in the city with nothing left to defend, he and Xian at last went to the hill behind and hanged themselves from the trees.

sentences.zh: 從死者數人，諸生初震、周大任兩家皆死之。

translations.literal: Those who followed in death were several; the student Chu Zhen and Zhou Daren—both households—all died.
translations.idiomatic: Several others died with them, and the households of the scholars Chu Zhen and Zhou Daren perished as well.

sentences.zh: 憲，浙江山陰人。

translations.literal: Xian, Zhejiang Shanyin person.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xian was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang.
